title.zh: 卷四十五 蜀書十五 鄧張宗楊傳
title.en: Volume 45: Book of Shu 15 - Biographies of Deng, Zhang, Zong, and Yang
title.raw: 卷四十五 蜀書十五 鄧張宗楊傳 Volume 45: Book of Shu 15 - Biographies of Deng, Zhang, Zong, and Yang

sentences.zh: 鄧芝字伯苗，義陽新野人，漢司徒禹之後也。

translations.literal: Deng Zhi, courtesy name Bomiao, was a man of Xinye in Yiyang, and a descendant of Yu, Minister of Education of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi, courtesy name Bomiao, came from Xinye in Yiyang and traced his line to Yu, who had served the Han as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 漢末入蜀，未見知待。

translations.literal: At the end of the Han he entered Shu and was not seen, known, or treated favorably.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Han he went into Shu, where no one took notice of him or gave him a post.

sentences.zh: 時益州從事張裕善相，芝往從之，裕謂芝曰：「君年過七十，位至大將軍，封侯。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yu, Adjunct of Yizhou, was skilled in physiognomy; Zhi went to follow him, and Yu said to Zhi: "You will pass seventy years of age, reach the position of Grand General, and be enfeoffed as a marquis."
translations.idiomatic: The Yizhou Adjunct Zhang Yu was a skilled physiognomist; Zhi sought him out, and Yu told him, "You will live past seventy, rise to Grand General, and receive a marquisate."

sentences.zh: 」芝聞巴西太守龐羲好士，往依焉。

translations.literal: " Zhi heard that Pang Xi, Administrator of Baxi, was fond of shi (talented men), and went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Pang Xi, the Administrator of Baxi, welcomed men of talent, Zhi went to join him.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，芝為郫邸閣督。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign pacified Yizhou, Zhi was Foreman of the Courier Hostel at Pi.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Sovereign secured Yizhou, Zhi served as foreman of the courier lodge at Pi.

sentences.zh: 先主出至郫，與語，大奇之，擢為郫令，遷廣漢太守。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign went out to Pi, spoke with him, greatly marveled at him, promoted him to magistrate of Pi, and moved him up to Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: The First Sovereign traveled to Pi, spoke with him, was deeply impressed, named him magistrate of Pi, and soon promoted him to Administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 所在清嚴有治績，入為尚書。

translations.literal: In the places where he served he was pure and strict and had administrative achievements; he entered as Minister Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he ran a tight, incorrupt administration and left a solid record, and he was recalled to court as Minister Secretary.

sentences.zh: 延熙六年，就遷為車騎將軍，後假節。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanxi he was moved up on the spot to General of Chariots and Cavalry, and afterward was granted the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 6 he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and later received the credential staff.

sentences.zh: 十一年，涪陵國人殺都尉反叛，芝率軍征討，即梟其渠帥，百姓安堵，

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the people of the Fuling princedom killed the Commandant and rebelled; Zhi led troops to campaign against them, immediately beheaded their chieftains, and the common people were secure and unmolested.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the people of Fuling killed their Commandant and rose in revolt; Zhi led a punitive expedition, executed their leaders at once, and the populace was left in peace.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：芝徵涪陵，見玄猿緣山。

translations.literal: 〈 The Huayang Guozhi says: When Zhi campaigned against Fuling, he saw a dark ape climbing the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang Guozhi records that on the Fuling campaign Zhi saw a dark ape moving along the mountainside.

sentences.zh: 芝性好弩，手自射猿，中之。

translations.literal: Zhi by nature was fond of crossbows; he personally shot the ape and hit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi loved the crossbow; he took aim himself and struck the ape.

sentences.zh: 猿拔其箭，卷木葉塞其創。

translations.literal: The ape pulled out the arrow, rolled tree leaves, and plugged its wound.
translations.idiomatic: The animal pulled the bolt free, rolled leaves together, and packed them into the wound.

sentences.zh: 芝曰：「嘻，吾違物之性，其將死矣！

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Hei, I have violated the nature of creatures; I suppose I am about to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi exclaimed, "I have violated the way of living things—I fear my end is near."

sentences.zh: 」一曰：芝見猿抱子在樹上，引弩射之，中猿母，其子為拔箭，以木葉塞創。

translations.literal: " Another version: Zhi saw an ape holding its child in a tree, drew his crossbow and shot it, hit the mother ape, and its child for its part pulled out the arrow and used tree leaves to plug the wound.
translations.idiomatic: Another account says Zhi saw a mother ape cradling her infant in a tree, shot her with his crossbow, and watched the young one pull out the bolt and stanch the wound with leaves.

sentences.zh: 芝乃嘆息，投弩水中，自知當死。〉

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon sighed, threw the crossbow into the water, and knew in himself he would die.〉
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, cast his crossbow into the water, and accepted that death was coming for him.〉

sentences.zh: 十四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 芝為

translations.literal: Zhi served as
translations.idiomatic: Zhi served as

translations.literal: Parenthetical: da (“great”).
translations.idiomatic: Editorial gloss: read da, “great,” immediately before the following phrase “general.”

sentences.zh: 將軍二十餘年，賞罰明斷，善卹卒伍。

translations.literal: general for more than twenty years; rewards and punishments were clear and decisive, and he was good at comforting rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: general for over two decades, with clear, firm discipline and a genuine concern for the men under his command.

sentences.zh: 身之衣食資仰於官，不苟素儉，然終不治私產，妻子不免飢寒，死之日家無餘財。

translations.literal: The resources for his clothing and food relied on official salary; he was not deliberately plain and austere, yet to the end he did not manage private property, and his wife and children did not avoid hunger and cold; on the day he died his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on his official stipend rather than affect austerity, yet he never built a private fortune; his family still knew want, and when he died there was nothing left in the house.

sentences.zh: 性剛簡，不飾意氣，不得士類之和。

translations.literal: By nature he was brusque and spare, did not adorn his temper, and did not obtain the harmony of the class of shi.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and undemonstrative, made no effort to smooth his manner, and won little goodwill among the literati.

sentences.zh: 於時人少所敬貴，唯器異姜維雲。

translations.literal: At the time few people respected and honored him; only he singularly regarded Jiang Wei as extraordinary, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Few of his contemporaries held him in esteem; alone among them he singled out Jiang Wei for exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 子良，襲爵，景耀中為尚書左選郎，晉朝廣漢太守。

translations.literal: His son Liang inherited the noble rank; in the Jingyao era he was Left Selection Gentleman among the Ministers; in the Jin dynasty he was Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liang inherited the title, served as Left Selection Gentleman under the Ministers during Jingyao, and under the Jin became Administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 張翼字伯恭，犍為武陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Bogong, was a man of Wuyang in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Bogong, was a native of Wuyang in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 高祖父司空浩，曾祖父廣陵太守綱，皆有名跡。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Hao was Minister of Works; his great-grandfather Gang was Administrator of Guangling; both had famous traces.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Hao had been Minister of Works and his great-grandfather Gang Administrator of Guangling; both left distinguished reputations.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：浩字叔明，治律、春秋，遊學京師，與廣漢鐔粲、漢中李郃、蜀郡張霸共結為友善。

translations.literal: 〈 The Yibu Qi Jiu Zhuan says: Hao, courtesy name Shuming, studied law and the Spring and Autumn Annals, traveled to study in the capital, and with Tan Can of Guanghan, Li He of Hanzhong, and Zhang Ba of Shujun together formed a bond of friendship. 〉
translations.idiomatic: The Yibu Qi Jiu Zhuan describes Hao (courtesy Shuming) as a student of law and the Spring and Autumn who studied in the capital and formed a close circle with Tan Can of Guanghan, Li He of Hanzhong, and Zhang Ba of Shu.〉

sentences.zh: 大將軍鄧騭闢浩，稍遷尚書僕射，出為彭城相，薦隱士閭丘邈等，徵拜廷尉。

translations.literal: Grand General Deng Zhi of the Later Han summoned Hao; he was gradually moved up to Vice Minister Secretary, went out as Chancellor of Pengcheng, recommended recluses such as Lüqiu Miao, and was summoned and appointed Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han grand marshal Deng Zhi summoned Hao to office; he rose to Vice Minister Secretary, then became chancellor of Pengcheng, where he recommended recluses including Lüqiu Miao, before being summoned back as Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 延光三年，安帝議廢太子，唯浩與太常桓焉、太僕來歷議以為不可。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanguang, when Emperor An discussed deposing the heir apparent, only Hao together with Minister of Ceremonies Huan Yan and Minister of Coachmen Lai Li debated holding that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanguang 3, when Emperor An debated deposing the crown prince, Hao, Huan Yan the Minister of Ceremonies, and Lai Li the Minister of Coachmen were the only ministers who argued against it.

sentences.zh: 順帝初立，拜浩司空，年八十三卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun was first enthroned, Hao was appointed Minister of Works; he died at age eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun came to the throne, Hao was named Minister of Works; he died at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 《續漢書》曰：綱字文紀，少以三公子經明行脩舉孝廉，不就司徒闢，以高第為侍御史。

translations.literal: The Xu Hanshu says: Gang, courtesy name Wenji, in youth was recommended Filial and Incorrupt as a classicist and man of good conduct among the three ducal sons; he did not take up the summons of the Minister of Education, and with a high ranking was made Attending Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu Hanshu says Gang, courtesy Wenji, was recommended Filial and Incorrupt in his youth as one of the classicist sons of the three dukes; he declined the Minister of Education’s summons and entered service with distinction as Attending Secretary.

sentences.zh: 漢安元年，拜光祿大夫，與侍中杜喬等八人同日受詔，持節分出，案行天下貪廉，墨綬有罪便收，刺史二千石以驛表聞，威惠清忠，名振郡國，號曰八雋。

translations.literal: In the first year of Han'an he was appointed Grand Counsellor and on the same day as eight others including Palace Attendant Du Qiao received edicts, each holding credentials and sent out separately to investigate greed and integrity in the empire; those with the black cord who were guilty were immediately taken in, and Inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials were reported by post; his might and favor were pure and loyal, his name shook commanderies and principalities, and they were called the Eight Exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: In Han'an 1 he became Grand Counsellor and, with Du Qiao and six other men, received commissions the same day to tour the realm with full credentials, arrest corrupt officials bearing the black ribbon, and memorialize on inspectors and two-thousand-bushel ranks by express courier. Their reputation for stern integrity spread through every commandery, and contemporaries dubbed them the Eight Exemplars.

sentences.zh: 是時，大將軍梁冀侵擾百姓，喬等七人皆奉命四出，唯綱獨埋車輪於洛陽都亭不去，曰：「豺狼當路，安問狐狸？

translations.literal: At that time Grand General Liang Ji harassed the common people; Qiao and the other seven all received orders and went out in four directions, but Gang alone buried his cart wheels at the metropolitan courier lodge in Luoyang and would not go, saying: "When wolves and jackals block the road, why ask about foxes?"
translations.idiomatic: While Grand General Liang Ji tyrannized the people, Du Qiao’s party of seven fanned out on imperial orders, but Gang alone drove to the Luoyang lodge, buried his wheels, and refused to move, declaring, "When wolves bar the road, who troubles himself over foxes?"

sentences.zh: 」遂上書曰：「大將軍梁冀、河南尹不疑，蒙外戚之援，荷國厚恩，以芻蕘之姿，安居阿保，不能敷揚五教，翼贊日月，而專為封豕長蛇，肆其貪饕，甘心好貨，縱恣無厭，多樹諂諛以害忠良，誠天威所不赦，大辟所宜加也。

translations.literal: " He thereupon submitted a memorial saying: "Grand General Liang Ji and Prefect of Henan Yin Bu Yi, relying on support as outer kin, have borne the state's thick kindness, yet with the posture of firewood-gatherers sit at ease as nursemaids; they cannot spread the Five Teachings or assist the sun and moon, but are wholly a great boar and long serpent, indulging their greed and gluttony, willingly loving goods, wantonly insatiable, planting many flatterers to harm the loyal and good—truly what heavenly majesty will not pardon and what great execution should be applied to."
translations.idiomatic: He then laid before the throne a bill of particulars: Liang Ji and the prefect Yin Bu Yi, though favored as imperial in-laws and laden with imperial grace, behaved like idle nursemaids instead of spreading the moral teachings or supporting the throne; they were ravening beasts—insatiably greedy, trafficking in flattery, and destroying good men—crimes no sovereign should forgive and worthy of the supreme penalty."

sentences.zh: 謹條其無君之心十五事於左，皆忠臣之所切齒也。

translations.literal: I respectfully list fifteen matters of his heart without regard for his ruler on the left; all are what loyal ministers gnash their teeth at.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully append fifteen counts of his disloyal designs; each would make a faithful minister grind his teeth in rage.

sentences.zh: 」書奏禦，京師震悚。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was presented to the imperial carriage, the capital trembled with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the emperor, the whole capital shook with apprehension.

sentences.zh: 時冀妹為皇后，內寵方盛，冀兄弟權重於人主，順帝雖知綱言不誣，然無心治冀。

translations.literal: At the time Ji's younger sister was empress, inner favor was just flourishing, and the weight of power of Ji's brothers was heavier than the ruler's; though Emperor Shun knew Gang's words were not false, yet he had no mind to punish Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji’s sister sat as empress, palace favor ran high, and the Liang brothers outweighed the throne; Emperor Shun knew Gang spoke the truth yet would not move against Ji.

sentences.zh: 冀深恨綱。

translations.literal: Ji deeply hated Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji nursed a bitter grudge against Gang.

sentences.zh: 會廣陵賊張嬰等眾數万人殺刺史二千石，冀欲陷綱，乃諷尚書以綱為廣陵太守；

translations.literal: When bandits of Guangling, Zhang Ying and others, a host of several tens of thousands, killed the Inspector and two-thousand-bushel officials, Ji wished to ruin Gang and therefore prompted the Minister Secretary to appoint Gang Administrator of Guangling;
translations.idiomatic: When tens of thousands of Guangling rebels under Zhang Ying murdered the provincial inspector and senior officials, Ji saw a chance to destroy Gang and had the Minister Secretary name him Administrator of Guangling;

sentences.zh: 若不為嬰所殺，則欲以法中之。

translations.literal: if he were not killed by Ying, then he wished to catch him in the law.
translations.idiomatic: if the bandits did not kill him, the law would be twisted to do it instead.

sentences.zh: 前太守往，輒多請兵，及綱受拜，詔問當得兵馬幾何，綱對曰無用兵馬，遂單車之官，徑詣嬰壘門，示以禍福。

translations.literal: Previous administrators on going out always requested many troops; when Gang received his appointment the edict asked how many troops and horses he ought to obtain, and Gang replied that he needed to use no troops or horses; he thereupon went to office with a single cart, went straight to the gate of Ying's fortress, and showed him disaster and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier appointees had demanded large escorts, but when the court asked Gang how many men he required, he answered none, drove alone to his post, rode straight to Zhang Ying’s camp, and laid out the consequences of resistance or submission.

sentences.zh: 嬰大驚懼，走欲閉門。

translations.literal: Ying was greatly alarmed and afraid, ran and wished to shut the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying panicked and ran to bar the gates.

sentences.zh: 綱又於門外罷遣吏兵，留所親者十餘人，以書語其長老素為嬰所信者，請與相見，問以本變，因示以詔恩，使還請嬰。

translations.literal: Gang again outside the gate dismissed and sent away clerks and soldiers, kept a little more than ten of those he was intimate with, used a letter to speak to the elders whom Ying had long trusted, asked to meet with them, asked them the origin of the uprising, thereby showed them the grace of the edict, and had them return to ask Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls Gang sent the escort away, kept a dozen trusted followers, wrote to the clan elders Zhang Ying respected, met them to learn how the revolt began, explained the emperor’s offer of mercy, and sent them back to bring Ying out.

sentences.zh: 嬰見綱意誠，即出見綱。

translations.literal: Ying saw Gang's intent was sincere and immediately came out to see Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Gang meant what he said, Ying came out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 綱延置上坐，問其疾苦，禮畢，乃謂之曰：「前後二千石，多非其人，杜塞國恩，肆其私求。

translations.literal: Gang led him in and seated him in the upper seat, asked his hardships and bitterness, and when the rites were finished then said to him: "Former and later two-thousand-bushel officials were mostly not the right men; they blocked the state's favor and indulged their private requests."
translations.idiomatic: Gang ushered him to the seat of honor, asked after the people’s hardships, and when the courtesies were done said, "Successive governors have mostly been the wrong men—throttling imperial kindness while serving private greed."

sentences.zh: 鄉郡遠，天子不能朝夕聞也，故民人相聚以避害。

translations.literal: Your commandery is distant and the Son of Heaven cannot hear morning and evening; therefore the people gathered together to avoid harm.
translations.idiomatic: Your lands lie far from the capital; the emperor cannot hear every grievance, so the people banded together simply to survive official abuse.

sentences.zh: 二千石信有罪矣；

translations.literal: The two-thousand-bushel officials truly had guilt;
translations.idiomatic: Those governors may indeed have been guilty;

sentences.zh: 為之者乃非義也。

translations.literal: what was done in response was not righteous.
translations.idiomatic: but armed resistance was still the wrong course.

sentences.zh: 忠臣不欺君以自榮，孝子不損父以求福，天子聖

translations.literal: Loyal ministers do not deceive the ruler to glorify themselves; filial sons do not harm their fathers to seek blessing; the Son of Heaven is sacred
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers do not lie to advance themselves; filial sons do not wound their fathers for gain; the Son of Heaven is a sage

translations.literal: Parenthetical: ren (“person”).
translations.idiomatic: Editorial gloss: ren completes the word shengren, “sage,” begun in the previous clause.

sentences.zh: ，欲文德以來之，故使太守來，思以爵祿相榮，不原以刑也。

translations.literal: , and wishes to draw them with civil virtue; therefore he sent an administrator to come, thinking to honor one another with rank and stipend, not originally intending to use punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Who means to win you with civil virtue rather than the sword. That is why he sent a governor—to honor you with rank and stipend, not to begin with the executioner’s block.

sentences.zh: 今誠轉禍為福之時也；

translations.literal: Now is truly the time to turn calamity into blessing;
translations.idiomatic: This is the moment to trade ruin for safety;

sentences.zh: 若聞義不服，天子赫然發怒，大兵雲合，豈不危乎！

translations.literal: if you hear righteousness and do not submit, when the Son of Heaven blazes with anger great troops will gather like clouds—how could it not be perilous!
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse a just settlement, the emperor’s wrath will fall and armies will mass like storm clouds—how could you escape disaster?

sentences.zh: 宜深計其利害。

translations.literal: You ought to calculate deeply the advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the cost carefully.

sentences.zh: 」嬰聞，泣曰：「荒裔愚人，數為二千石所侵枉，不堪其困，故遂相聚偷生。

translations.literal: " Ying heard and wept, saying: "We foolish men of the wild border have repeatedly been wronged and bent by two-thousand-bushel officials, could not endure their oppression, therefore gathered together to steal life."
translations.idiomatic: Ying wept and replied, "We are ignorant folk on the frontier, driven to desperation by one corrupt governor after another; we banded together only to cling to life."

sentences.zh: 明府仁及草木，乃嬰等更生之澤，但恐投兵之日，不免孥戮耳。

translations.literal: Your honor's benevolence reaches even plants and trees; it is the moisture that gives Ying and others another life; only we fear that on the day we lay down weapons we will not avoid slaughtering wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Your compassion touches even the grass, and it would give us a second life—yet we dread that the day we disarm will be the day our families are executed."

sentences.zh: 」綱曰：「豈其然乎！

translations.literal: " Gang said: "How could it be so!"
translations.idiomatic: Gang answered, "Nothing of the sort!"

sentences.zh: 要之以天地，誓之以日月，方當相顯以爵位，何禍之有乎？

translations.literal: I bind you by heaven and earth and swear by sun and moon; in due course I will make one another conspicuous with rank and position—what calamity could there be!"
translations.idiomatic: I swear by heaven, earth, sun, and moon that you will be raised to honor with titles and stipends—what harm could come to you?"

sentences.zh: 」嬰曰：「苟赦其罪，得全首領以就農畝，則抱戴沒齒，爵祿非所望也。

translations.literal: " Ying said: "If you pardon their crimes and let them preserve their heads whole to go to the farm fields, then we will embrace and bear gratitude to the end of our teeth; rank and stipend are not what we hope for."
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "If you spare our lives and let us return to the plough, we will be grateful to our dying day; titles and salaries are more than we dare hope for."

sentences.zh: 」嬰雖為大賊，起於狂暴，自以為必死，及得綱言，曠然開明，乃辭還營。

translations.literal: " Ying though he was a great bandit had risen in violence and fury, reckoned himself sure to die; when he obtained Gang's words he was suddenly enlightened, bowed in farewell, and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ying had risen as a desperate outlaw and expected death, Gang’s words opened his eyes; he took his leave and went back to the camp.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂將所部萬餘人，與妻子麵縛詣綱降。

translations.literal: The next day he thereupon led his command of more than ten thousand together with wives and children, bound face-to-back with rope, and came to Gang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he brought more than ten thousand followers, with wives and children, hands tied behind their backs, and surrendered to Gang.

sentences.zh: 綱悉釋縛慰納，謂嬰曰：「卿諸人一旦解散，方垂蕩然，當條名上之，必受封賞。

translations.literal: Gang loosed all bonds, comforted and accepted them, and said to Ying: "If you gentlemen once disband, the region will just hang swept clear; I ought to list names and report upward; you are sure to receive enfeoffment and reward."
translations.idiomatic: Gang cut their bonds, reassured them, and said, "Disband your host and the countryside will be quiet again; I will list your names for the throne, and rewards will follow."

sentences.zh: 」嬰曰：「乞歸故業，不原以穢名汙明時也。

translations.literal: " Ying said: "We beg to return to former occupations; we do not wish to use foul names to stain a bright age."
translations.idiomatic: Ying replied, "We ask only to resume our old trades; we would not stain this enlightened reign with the stigma of banditry."

sentences.zh: 」綱以其至誠，乃各從其意，親為安處居宅。

translations.literal: " Gang because of their utmost sincerity then followed each man's intent and personally for them settled dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by their sincerity, Gang granted every request and personally saw to their housing.

sentences.zh: 子弟欲為吏者，隨才任職，欲為民者，勸以農桑，田業並豐，南州晏然。

translations.literal: Sons and younger kin who wished to be clerks were appointed according to talent; those who wished to be commoners were urged in farming and silk; fields and occupations were both abundant, and the southern province was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Sons who wanted office received posts suited to their abilities; those who preferred farming were settled on the land with seed and silkworms until fields flourished again and the south grew calm.

sentences.zh: 論功，綱當封，為冀所遏絕，故不得侯。

translations.literal: When merit was discussed Gang ought to have been enfeoffed, but was blocked and cut off by Ji, therefore could not obtain a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: By rights Gang should have been ennobled for this, but Liang Ji blocked the award and he never received a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 天子美其功，徵欲用之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven praised his achievement and summoned him intending to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his service and summoned him to court for higher office.

sentences.zh: 嬰等上書，乞留在郡二歲。

translations.literal: Ying and others submitted memorials begging to be allowed to remain in the commandery two years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying and his followers petitioned that Gang be allowed to stay another two years as their governor.

sentences.zh: 建康元年，病卒官，時年三十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiankang he died of illness in office; at the time his age was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiankang 1 he died of illness in post, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 嬰等三百餘人，皆衰杖送綱喪至洛陽，葬訖，為起塚立祠，四時奉祭，思慕如喪考妣。

translations.literal: More than three hundred of Ying and others all with mourning staff escorted Gang's funeral to Luoyang; when burial was finished they for him raised a mound and established a shrine, made offerings in the four seasons, and longed for him as if mourning father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: Over three hundred of Ying’s men wore mourning and carried staffs all the way to Luoyang for Gang’s funeral; after the burial they built him a tomb and a shrine, kept the seasonal sacrifices, and mourned him as they would their own parents.

sentences.zh: 天子追念不已，下詔褒揚，除一子為郎。〉

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven could not stop remembering him, issued an edict to praise and display him, and appointed one son Gentleman.〉
translations.idiomatic: The court could not forget him, issued a decree of commendation, and ennobled one of his sons as a Gentleman.〉

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，領牧，翼為書佐。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign pacified Yizhou and held the shepherdcy, Yi was a clerical aide.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Sovereign took Yizhou and assumed the shepherd’s staff, Yi served him as a clerical aide.

sentences.zh: 建安末，舉孝廉，為江陽長，徙涪陵令，遷梓潼太守，累遷至廣漢、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jian'an era he was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, became magistrate of Jiangyang, was moved to magistrate of Fuling, was moved up to Administrator of Zitong, and by cumulative promotion reached Administrator of Guanghan and of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jian’an period he was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, served as magistrate of Jiangyang and then Fuling, rose to Administrator of Zitong, and by steady promotion became Administrator of both Guanghan and Shu commanderies.

sentences.zh: 建興九年，為庲降都督、綏南中郎將。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jianxing he was Area Commander of Laixiang and General Who Pacifies the South of the Center.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 9 he was named Area Commander at Laixiang and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 翼性持法嚴，不得殊俗之歡心。

translations.literal: Yi by nature upheld the law strictly and did not obtain the joyful hearts of different customs.
translations.idiomatic: Yi enforced the law with a heavy hand and never won the affection of the local peoples.

sentences.zh: 耆率劉冑背叛作亂，翼舉兵討冑。

translations.literal: The native elder Liu Zhou rebelled and raised disturbance; Yi raised troops to punish Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled; Yi took the field against him.

sentences.zh: 冑未破，會被徵當還，群下咸以為宜便馳騎即罪，翼曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhou was not yet broken when he happened to be summoned and ought to return; his subordinates all thought he ought immediately to ride post-horses to answer for his crime, but Yi said: "It is not so."
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhou was crushed, orders arrived recalling Yi to court; his officers urged him to gallop straight to the capital and answer for any fault, but Yi said, "That would be wrong."

sentences.zh: 吾以蠻夷蠢動，不稱職故還耳，然代人未至，吾方臨戰場，當運糧積穀，為滅賊之資，豈可以黜退之故而廢公家之務乎？

translations.literal: I am recalled because the barbarians stirred stupidly and I was not competent for the post, yet my replacement has not arrived; I am just on the battlefield and ought to transport grain and pile up grain as capital to destroy the bandits—how can I, on account of demotion and recall, abandon the state's business!"
translations.idiomatic: I am recalled because the tribes rose and I failed in my post, but my successor is not here yet. I still stand on a battlefield—I must move grain and fill the granaries as the means to finish these rebels. How could I abandon public duty because of a personal setback?"

sentences.zh: 」於是統攝不懈，代到乃發。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he directed and grasped tirelessly; when the replacement arrived then he set out.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore kept command without slackening and only departed when his replacement arrived.

sentences.zh: 馬忠因其成基以破殄冑，丞相亮聞而善之。

translations.literal: Ma Zhong because of the foundation he had completed used it to break and exterminate Zhou; Chancellor Liang heard and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhong built on the position Yi had secured to destroy Liu Zhou; Chancellor Zhuge Liang heard the story and approved.

sentences.zh: 亮出武功，以翼為前軍都督，領扶風太守。

translations.literal: When Liang went out to Wugong, he made Yi Colonel of the Van and concurrent Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: On the Wugong expedition Liang named Yi commander of the van and concurrent Administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，拜前領軍，追論討劉冑功，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: When Liang died he was appointed former Commander of the Center Army; retroactively for merit in attacking Liu Zhou he was granted noble rank as village marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang’s death he became Commander of the Center Army; his later success against Liu Zhou earned him a village marquisate inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 延熙元年，入為尚書，稍遷督建威，假節，進封都亭侯，征西大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxi he entered as Minister, was gradually moved up to supervise Jianwei, was granted the staff of authority, advanced enfeoffment to village marquis of the capital at the pavilion, and General Who Conquers the West.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 1 he entered the ministry, rose to supervise Jianwei with the credential staff, was advanced to village marquis at the metropolitan pavilion, and became General Who Conquers the West.

sentences.zh: 十八年，與衛將軍姜維俱還成都。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he together with Guards General Jiang Wei both returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of the reign he returned to Chengdu with Guards General Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 維議復出軍，唯翼廷爭，以為國小民勞，不宜黷武。

translations.literal: Wei debated again leading the army out; only Yi disputed in court, holding that the state was small and the people weary, and that it was not fitting to indulge in arms.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei proposed another northern campaign, Yi alone argued in open court that the realm was too small and the people too exhausted for further war.

sentences.zh: 維不聽，將翼等行，進翼位鎮南大將軍。

translations.literal: Wei did not listen, took Yi and others on the march, and advanced Yi's position to General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ignored him, took Yi with the army, and promoted him to General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 維至狄道，大破魏雍州刺史王經，經眾死於洮水者以萬計。

translations.literal: When Wei reached Didao he greatly defeated Wang Jing, Inspector of Yongzhou of Wei, and of Jing's host those who died in the Tao water were reckoned by the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At Didao Wei shattered Wei’s Inspector of Yongzhou, Wang Jing; tens of thousands of Jing’s men drowned in the Tao.

sentences.zh: 翼曰：「可止矣，不宜復進，進或毀此大功。

translations.literal: Yi said: "One may stop; it is not fitting to advance further; advancing might ruin this great achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Yi urged him to halt: "Press no further—you could throw away this victory."

sentences.zh: 」維大怒。

translations.literal: " Wei was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Wei flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 曰：「為蛇畫足。

translations.literal: He said: "Drawing feet on a snake."
translations.idiomatic: He snapped, "You are painting feet on a snake."

sentences.zh: 」維竟圍經於狄道，城不能克。

translations.literal: " Wei in the end besieged Jing at Didao but could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei went on to besiege Wang Jing at Didao and failed to storm the walls.

sentences.zh: 自翼建異論，維心與翼不善，然常牽率同行，翼亦不得已而往。

translations.literal: From the time Yi set forth divergent debate Wei's heart toward Yi was not good, yet he often dragged and led him to go together; Yi likewise had no choice but to go.
translations.idiomatic: After that public disagreement Wei bore Yi a grudge yet kept dragging him on every expedition, and Yi had little choice but to follow.

sentences.zh: 景耀二年，遷左車騎將軍，領冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyao he was moved to General of Chariots and Cavalry of the Left and concurrent Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyao 2 he became General of Chariots and Cavalry of the Left and nominal Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 六年，與維咸在劍閣，共詣降鍾會於涪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he and Wei were both at Jiange and together went to surrender to Zhong Hui at Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he and Wei were holding Jiange when they went together to surrender to Zhong Hui at Fu.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，隨會至成都，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he followed Hui to Chengdu and was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month he accompanied Hui to Chengdu and died in the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：翼子微，篤志好學，官至廣漢太守。〉

translations.literal: 〈 The Huayang Guozhi says: Yi's son Wei was devoted in intent and fond of study; his office reached Administrator of Guanghan.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang Guozhi adds that Yi's son Wei was a devoted scholar who rose to Administrator of Guanghan.〉

sentences.zh: 宗預字德艷，南陽安眾人也。

translations.literal: Zong Yu, courtesy name Deyan, was a man of Anzhong in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yu, courtesy name Deyan, came from Anzhong in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 建安中，隨張飛入蜀。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an era he followed Zhang Fei into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jian’an years he followed Zhang Fei into Shu.

sentences.zh: 建興初，丞相亮以為主簿，遷參軍右中郎將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianxing Chancellor Liang made him chief clerk and moved him up to Army Advisor and General of the Right Center.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianxing Chancellor Zhuge Liang appointed him chief clerk, then promoted him to army adviser and General of the Right Center.

sentences.zh: 及亮卒，吳慮魏或承衰取蜀，增巴丘守兵萬人，一欲以為救援，二欲以事分割也。

translations.literal: When Liang died, Wu feared that Wei might take advantage of decline to seize Shu, increased garrison troops at Baqiu by ten thousand, partly wishing to use them as relief, partly wishing to use the affair to partition.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang’s death Wu feared that Wei might strike Shu in her weakness and posted ten thousand extra troops at Baqiu—partly as a relief force, partly as leverage for a partition of the west.

sentences.zh: 蜀聞之，亦益永安之守，以防非常。

translations.literal: Shu hearing of it likewise increased the garrison at Yong'an to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Shu responded by reinforcing Yong’an against any surprise from the east.

sentences.zh: 預將命使吳，孫權問預曰：「東之與西，譬猶一家，而聞西更增白帝之守，何也？

translations.literal: When Zong Yu bore orders as envoy to Wu, Sun Quan asked him, saying: "East and west are like one household, yet I hear the west has again increased the garrison at Baidi—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Yu went to Wu on a mission, Sun Quan asked him, "We east and you west are supposed to be one family—so why have I heard that Shu has strengthened the garrison at Baidi?"

sentences.zh: 」預對曰：「臣以為東益巴丘之戍，西增白帝之守，皆事勢宜然，俱不足以相問也。

translations.literal: " Yu replied, saying: "Your servant considers that the east increasing the guard at Baqiu and the west increasing the guard at Baidi are both what the situation of affairs calls for; neither is enough to warrant mutual questioning."
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered, "On our side we strengthened Yong’an when you reinforced Baqiu; both moves fit the circumstances. Neither side has anything to reproach the other about."

sentences.zh: 」權大笑，嘉其抗直，甚愛待之，見敬亞於鄧芝、費禕。

translations.literal: " Quan laughed greatly, praised his blunt forthrightness, treated him with great love and regard, and the respect shown him was next after Deng Zhi and Fei Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Quan roared with approval, praised his plainspoken courage, and favored him almost as highly as Deng Zhi or Fei Yi.

sentences.zh: 遷為侍中，徙尚書。

translations.literal: He was moved up to Palace Attendant and transferred to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, then transferred into the ministry as a regular minister.

sentences.zh: 咸熙元年春，化、預俱內徙洛陽，道病卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xianxi, Hua and Yu were both moved inward to Luoyang; on the road he died of illness. (The text reads “Hua,” i.e. Liao Hua.)
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xianxi 1, Liao Hua and Zong Yu were both ordered to relocate to Luoyang; Yu died of illness on the journey.

sentences.zh: 楊戲字文然，犍為武陽人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xi, courtesy name Wenran, was a man of Wuyang in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xi, courtesy name Wenran, came from Wuyang in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 少與巴西程祁公弘、巴郡楊汰季儒、蜀郡張表伯達並知名。

translations.literal: In youth together with Cheng Qi of Baxi, style name Gonghong, Yang Tai of Bajun, style name Jiru, and Zhang Biao of Shujun, style name Boda, he was equally renowned.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was as well known as Cheng Qi of Baxi (courtesy Gonghong), Yang Tai of Ba (courtesy Jiru), and Zhang Biao of Shu (courtesy Boda).

sentences.zh: 戲每推祁以為冠首，丞相亮深識之。

translations.literal: Xi always pushed Qi to be crown head; Chancellor Liang deeply recognized this.
translations.idiomatic: Xi always ranked Cheng Qi first among them, and Chancellor Zhuge Liang took careful note of him.

sentences.zh: 戲年二十餘，從州書佐為督軍從事，職典刑獄，論法決疑，號為平當，府闢為屬主簿。

translations.literal: When Xi was a little more than twenty, from provincial clerical aide he became Army Supervisor Adjunct, his duty being to oversee criminal cases, discuss law and decide doubts, and he was styled fair and fitting; the office summoned him as subordinate chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties he rose from a provincial clerk to Army Supervisor Adjunct, where he handled penal matters, settled legal doubts, and earned a reputation for evenhanded justice; the administration then appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，為尚書右選部郎，刺史蔣琬請為治中從事史。

translations.literal: When Liang died he became Gentleman of the Right Selection Bureau among the Ministers; Inspector Jiang Wan requested him as Adjunct Clerk for the Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang’s death he served as a gentleman in the ministry’s right selection bureau; Inspector Jiang Wan then asked him to take the post of headquarters adjutant.

sentences.zh: 琬以大將軍開府，又闢為東曹掾，遷南中郎參軍，副貳庲降都督，領建寧太守。

translations.literal: When Wan as Grand General opened a bureau, he again summoned him as Eastern Bureau Clerk, moved him up to Army Advisor to the General of the Southern Center, as deputy seconded to the Area Commander of Laixiang, and concurrent Administrator of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan opened his grand-general’s bureau he took Xi on as Eastern Bureau clerk, then promoted him to adviser to the southern-center general, deputy to the Laixiang area commander, and acting Administrator of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 以疾徵還成都，拜護軍監軍，出領梓潼太守，入為射聲校尉，所在清約不煩。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was summoned back to Chengdu, was appointed Protector of the Army Supervisor of the Army, went out to concurrent Administrator of Zitong, entered as Colonel of Archers Who Shoot at a Sound, and in the places where he served was pure and abstemious and not troublesome.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to Chengdu on grounds of illness, he became Protector and army supervisor, then left office to govern Zitong, returned as Colonel of Archers Who Shoot at a Sound, and everywhere left a record for clean, unburdensome rule.

sentences.zh: 延熙二十年，隨大將軍姜維出軍至芒水。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yanxi he followed Grand General Jiang Wei in leading the army out as far as Mangshui.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 20 he marched with Grand General Jiang Wei’s host to Mangshui.

sentences.zh: 戲素心不服維，酒後言笑，每有傲弄之辭。

translations.literal: Xi in his plain heart did not submit to Wei; after wine in speech and laughter there were often arrogant mocking phrases.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had never respected Jiang Wei in his heart; over wine his talk often turned sarcastic and dismissive.

sentences.zh: 維外寬內忌，意不能堪，軍還，有司承旨奏戲，免為庶人。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei outwardly was broad inwardly was jealous; his intent could not bear it; when the army returned, the relevant offices receiving his intent memorialized against Xi, and he was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei was outwardly magnanimous but inwardly touchy; when the army came home his partisans memorialized against Xi, who was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 後景耀四年卒。

translations.literal: Afterward in the fourth year of Jingyao he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingyao 4.

sentences.zh: 戲性雖簡惰省略，未嘗以甘言加人，過情接物。

translations.literal: Although Xi's nature was simple, lazy, and abbreviated, he never used sweet words to impose on people or exceeded feeling in receiving things.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was terse and sparing of words—he never flattered anyone or put on airs in company.

sentences.zh: 書符指事，希有盈紙。

translations.literal: In writing talismans and pointing to affairs, rarely was there a full sheet of paper.
translations.idiomatic: His letters and memoranda were so brief they seldom filled a page.

sentences.zh: 然篤於舊故，居誠存厚。

translations.literal: Yet he was earnest toward old associations, dwelt in sincerity and preserved generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet toward old friends he was steadfastly loyal and warm.

sentences.zh: 與巴西韓儼、黎韜童幼相親厚，後儼痼疾廢頓，韜無行見捐，戲經紀振卹，恩好如初。

translations.literal: With Han Yan of Baxi and Li Tao of Li he was close and thick from boyhood; afterward Yan with chronic illness was crippled and halted, Tao with no conduct was cast aside, but Xi managed affairs and relieved and aided them, and grace and friendship were as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He had been close to Han Yan of Baxi and Li Tao since childhood; when Han was crippled by chronic illness and Li was shunned for scandalous behavior, Xi still managed their affairs and gave them relief until the old affection was restored.

sentences.zh: 又時人謂譙周無當世才，少歸敬者，唯戲重之，嘗稱曰：「吾等後世，終自不如此長兒也。

translations.literal: Moreover people of the time said Qiao Zhou had no talent for the present age, and few submitted respect to him; only Xi esteemed him and once praised, saying: "We in later generations will in the end not be like this grown son."
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries dismissed Qiao Zhou as lacking practical talent, and few deferred to him; Xi alone held him in esteem and once remarked, "Men like us will never match that man in the long run."

sentences.zh: 」有識以此貴戲。

translations.literal: " Men of insight on this account honored Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful men prized Xi all the more for that.

sentences.zh: 張表有威儀風觀，始名位與戲齊，後至尚書，督庲降後將軍，先戲沒。

translations.literal: Zhang Biao had imposing bearing and air; at first fame and position were equal with Xi; afterward he reached Minister, supervised Rear General of Laixiang, and died before Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao carried himself with dignity; he had once stood on a par with Xi, rose to minister, and became Rear General under the Laixiang command—yet he died before Xi did.

sentences.zh: 祁、汰各早死。

translations.literal: Qi and Tai each died early.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qi and Yang Tai both died young.

sentences.zh: 〈戲同縣後進有李密者，字令伯。

translations.literal: 〈 Among later youths of the same county as Xi was one Li Mi, courtesy name Lingbo.
translations.idiomatic: Among the younger men of Xi’s county was Li Mi, courtesy name Lingbo.

sentences.zh: 《華陽國志》曰：密祖父光，硃提太守。

translations.literal: The Huayang Guozhi says: Mi's grandfather Guang was Administrator of Zhuti.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang Guozhi states that Mi’s grandfather Guang had been Administrator of Zhuti.

sentences.zh: 父早亡。

translations.literal: His father died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was still a child.

sentences.zh: 母何氏，更適人。

translations.literal: His mother, née He, remarried to another man.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, the Lady He, remarried.

sentences.zh: 密見養於祖母。

translations.literal: Mi was seen and raised by his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought up by his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 治春秋左氏傳，博覽多所通涉，機警辯捷。

translations.literal: He studied the Zuo commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, broadly read and had many thorough crossings, was alert and quick in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Zuo commentary to the Spring and Autumn, read widely, and was quick-witted in debate.

sentences.zh: 事祖母以孝聞，其侍疾則泣涕側息，日夜不解帶，膳飲湯藥，必自口嘗。

translations.literal: Serving his grandmother he was famed for filial piety; when she was ill he wept tears and lay on his side without breath, day and night did not undo his belt, and for meals, drink, soup, and medicine he always personally tasted them in his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: His care for her won him a name for filial piety: when she fell ill he wept beside her couch, went without undressing night and day, and tasted every dish and dose of medicine himself.

sentences.zh: 本郡禮命不應，州闢從事尚書郎，大將軍主簿，太子洗馬，奉使聘吳。

translations.literal: The commandery's ritual summons he did not answer; the province summoned him as Adjunct, Gentleman of the Ministers, chief clerk to the Grand General, and Heir-Apparent's concubine's son horsewasher, and he bore orders as envoy to woo Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He declined local appointment but accepted successive posts as provincial adjutant, gentleman in the ministry, chief clerk to the grand general, and heir-apparent attendant, and was sent on a mission to Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳主問蜀馬多少，對曰：「官用有餘，人間自足。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu asked how many horses Shu had; he replied, saying: "For official use there is surplus; among the people it is self-sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu sovereign asked how many horses Shu possessed, Mi answered, "The government stables have enough, and the people have all they need."

sentences.zh: 」吳主與群臣汎論道義，謂寧為人弟，密曰：「原為人兄矣。

translations.literal: " The ruler of Wu with his ministers broadly discussed the Way and righteousness, saying it was better to be another's younger brother; Mi said: "I would rather be another's elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wu’s court debated whether it was better to be a younger or an elder brother in the moral sense, Mi said he would rather be the elder.

sentences.zh: 」吳主曰：「何以為兄？

translations.literal: " The ruler of Wu said: "By what is one an elder brother?"
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign asked what he meant by choosing elder brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 」密曰：「為兄供養之日長。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Being an elder brother, the days of providing support are long."
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied, "An elder brother bears the burden of support for far longer."

sentences.zh: 」吳主及群臣皆稱善。

translations.literal: " The ruler of Wu and the ministers all praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler and his courtiers applauded the answer.

sentences.zh: 蜀平後，征西將軍鄧艾聞其名，請為主簿，及書招，欲與相見，皆不往。

translations.literal: After Shu was pacified, Deng Ai, General Who Conquers the West, heard his name, requested him as chief clerk, and when he wrote summoning him and wished to meet with him, he all did not go.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Shu, Deng Ai the western conqueror general, hearing of him, offered him the post of chief clerk and wrote inviting a meeting; Mi declined every overture.

sentences.zh: 以祖母年老，心在色養。

translations.literal: Because his grandmother was aged in years, his heart was in "color" nurturing (i.e. joyful support).
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother was old, and his whole mind was set on caring for her in person.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝立太子，徵為太子洗馬，詔書累下，郡縣偪遣，於是密上書曰：「臣以險釁，夙遭閔兇，生孩六月，慈父見背，行年四歲，舅奪母志。

translations.literal: When Jin Emperor Wu established the heir apparent, he was summoned as Heir-Apparent's concubine's son horsewasher; edicts repeatedly came down, commanderies and counties pressed and sent him; thereupon Mi submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant by hazard and misfortune early met with sorrowful evil; at six months after birth the kindly father turned his back; at the fourth year of age the maternal uncle seized the mother's intent."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin named a crown prince, Mi was summoned as heir-apparent attendant; repeated edicts and county pressure forced the issue, and he presented the memorial that begins, "Your servant has had a hard fate: bereavement came early—my father died before I was a year old, and at four my uncle forced my mother to remarry."

sentences.zh: 祖母劉，愍臣孤弱，躬見撫養。

translations.literal: Grandmother Liu pitied your servant orphaned and weak and personally saw to raising him.
translations.idiomatic: My grandmother, the Lady Liu, took pity on my orphan weakness and raised me with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 臣少多疾病，九歲不行，零丁孤苦，至於成立，既無伯叔，終鮮兄弟，門衰祚薄，晚有兒息。

translations.literal: Your servant in youth had many illnesses; at nine sui could not walk; alone and solitary bitter and orphaned, until reaching establishment; since he had neither uncles nor in the end few brothers, the gate declined and fortune was thin, and late he had a son's breath.
translations.idiomatic: I was often ill as a child and could not walk until I was nine; I grew up alone, without uncles or brothers, my house declined and heirs came late.

sentences.zh: 外無期功強近之親，內無應門五尺之童，煢煢孑立，形影相吊。

translations.literal: Outside there were no strong-near kin of one-year or nine-month mourning; inside there was no five-foot child to answer the gate; alone he stood, body and shadow consoled each other.
translations.idiomatic: I had no kinsmen near enough to lean on, no servant even tall enough to answer the door—I stood utterly alone, only my shadow for company.

sentences.zh: 而劉早嬰疾病，常在床蓐，臣侍湯藥，未曾廢離。

translations.literal: But Liu early was bound by illness, constantly on bed and mat; your servant attended soup and medicine, never once ceased or left.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady Liu has long been bedridden; I have nursed her without a day’s absence.

sentences.zh: 逮奉聖朝，沐浴清化，前太守臣逵察臣孝廉，後刺史臣榮舉臣秀才，臣以供養無主，辭不赴命。

translations.literal: Until receiving the sage court, bathing in clear transformation, the former Administrator your servant Kui examined your servant Filial and Incorrupt, afterward the Inspector your servant Rong raised your servant Xiucai; your servant because support had no master declined and did not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Under this enlightened reign I was bathed in grace: Governor Kui nominated me Filial and Incorrupt, then Inspector Rong nominated me as a cultivated talent; each time I pleaded that no one else could care for my grandmother and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 詔書特下，拜臣郎中，尋蒙國恩，除臣洗馬，猥以微賤，當侍東宮，非臣隕首所能上報。

translations.literal: An edict especially came down, appointed your servant Gentleman of the Interior; soon he received state grace, was appointed your servant horsewasher; meanly with base lowliness, ought to attend the Eastern Palace; it is not what your servant smashing his head could repay upward.
translations.idiomatic: Special edicts made me a gentleman of the interior, then heir-apparent attendant—offices a man as humble as I could never repay even with my life.

sentences.zh: 臣具表聞，辭不就職。

translations.literal: Your servant fully set forth in memorial and heard, declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: I laid the whole case before the throne and begged leave not to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 詔書切峻，責臣逋慢，郡縣偪迫，催臣上道，州司臨門，急於星火。

translations.literal: The edict was cutting and severe, blamed your servant for fleeing and slowness; commanderies and counties pressed and compelled, urged your servant on the road; the provincial office came to the gate, more urgent than sparks and fire.
translations.idiomatic: The court’s tone turned harsh, accusing me of evasion; county and prefecture hounded me onto the road, and provincial officers stood at my gate as pressing as fire.

sentences.zh: 臣欲奉詔奔馳，則劉病日篤，苟順私情，則告訴不許，臣之進退，實為狼狽。

translations.literal: Your servant wished to receive the edict and gallop off, then Liu's illness daily grew grave; if he followed private feeling, then complaint was not permitted; your servant's advance and retreat were truly wolf and badger (i.e. caught between).
translations.idiomatic: If I obey the summons my grandmother’s illness grows worse; if I yield to family feeling the law will not hear my plea—I am caught on every side.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖朝以孝治天下，凡在故老，猶蒙矜愍，況臣孤苦，特為尤甚。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself and consider: the sage court by filial piety governs the empire; all who are old still receive pity; how much more your servant orphaned and bitter, especially is it extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin governs all under heaven by filial piety; even common elders receive compassion, and my case is more desperate than theirs.

sentences.zh: 且臣少仕偽朝，歷職郎署，本圖宦達，不矜名節。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant in youth served the false court, passed through offices in the gentleman ranks, originally planned official advancement, did not pride himself on name and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I once served Shu in petty clerkships, seeking only a career, not a reputation for purity.

sentences.zh: 今臣亡國賤俘，至微至陋，猥蒙拔擢，寵命優渥，豈敢盤桓，有所希冀？

translations.literal: Now your servant is a destroyed-state base captive, extremely mean and extremely low; meanly receiving promotion and selection, favoring commands are generous and thick—how dare he hesitate and have something he hopes for?
translations.idiomatic: Now I am a captive of a fallen state, mean and obscure; that Your Majesty should honor me so—how could I linger out of ambition?

sentences.zh: 但以劉日薄西山，氣息奄奄，人命危淺，朝不慮夕。

translations.literal: But because Liu's sun presses the western mountain, breath gasps faintly, human life is perilous and shallow, morning does not consider evening.
translations.idiomatic: But the Lady Liu is like the setting sun—each breath may be her last; she may not survive the day.

sentences.zh: 臣無祖母，無以至今日，祖母無臣，亦無以終餘年，母孫二人，更相為命，是以區區不敢廢遠。

translations.literal: Your servant without grandmother had no means to reach this day; grandmother without your servant also had no means to finish remaining years; mother and grandson two persons mutually are each other's life; therefore in petty earnestness he dare not abandon distance.
translations.idiomatic: Without my grandmother I would not be alive; without me she cannot live out her years—we sustain each other, which is why I cannot leave her side.

sentences.zh: 臣今年四十有四，祖母劉今年九十有六，是臣盡節於陛下之日長，報養劉之日短也。

translations.literal: Your servant this year is forty-four; grandmother Liu this year is ninety-six; this is the day your servant exhausts integrity toward Your Majesty is long, the day he repays and nurtures Liu is short.
translations.idiomatic: I am forty-four and she ninety-six: the years in which I might serve Your Majesty will be many, but the days left to repay her are few.

sentences.zh: 烏鳥私情，原乞終養。

translations.literal: The black bird's private feeling; I beg to finish nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: Even crows repay their parents; I beg leave to nurse her to the end.

sentences.zh: 臣之辛苦，非徒蜀之人士及二州牧伯所見明知，皇天后土，實所共鑑。

translations.literal: Your servant's hardship and bitterness is not only what Shu’s men of affairs and the two provinces' shepherds and elders saw and clearly knew; August Heaven and Later Earth truly together mirror it.
translations.idiomatic: My plight is plain to every man in Shu and to the governors of Liang and Yi; Heaven and Earth are witness.

sentences.zh: 原陛下矜愍愚誠，聽臣微志，庶劉僥倖，保卒餘年。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty pity foolish sincerity, hear your servant's slight intent, perhaps Liu by luck may preserve and finish remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to pity this honest fool, grant my humble wish, and let the Lady Liu live out whatever years remain to her.

sentences.zh: 臣生當隕首，死當結草，臣不勝犬馬怖懼之情！

translations.literal: Your servant in life ought to smash his head; in death ought to tie grass; your servant cannot bear the dog-and-horse fear and dread!
translations.idiomatic: Living, I will lay down my life for you; dead, I would tie the knot of grass—such is the trembling devotion of your dog-and-horse servant!"

sentences.zh: 」武帝覽表曰：「密不空有名也。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu reading the memorial said: "Mi is not empty of name."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu read the petition and said, "This man’s fame is no hollow thing."

sentences.zh: 」嘉其誠款，賜奴婢二人，下郡縣供養其祖母奉膳。

translations.literal: " He praised his sincere earnestness, granted two slave girls, and ordered commanderies and counties to support and nurture his grandmother with provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Mi’s sincerity with two bondmaids and ordered the local authorities to supply his grandmother’s meals.

sentences.zh: 及祖母卒，服終，從尚書郎為河內溫縣令，政化嚴明。

translations.literal: When his grandmother died and mourning was finished, from Gentleman of the Ministers he became magistrate of Wen county in Henei; administration and transformation were strict and bright.
translations.idiomatic: After her death and the end of mourning he left the ministry for the magistracy of Wen in Henei, where his government was noted for severity and clarity.

sentences.zh: 中山諸王每過溫縣，必責求供給，溫吏民患之。

translations.literal: The various kings of Zhongshan whenever passing Wen county always demanded and sought supplies; Wen clerks and people were troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the princes of Zhongshan passed through Wen they demanded lavish hospitality, to the misery of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 及密至，中山王過縣，欲求芻茭薪蒸，密箋引高祖過沛，賓禮老幼，桑梓之供，一無煩擾，「伏惟明王孝思惟則，動識先戒，本國望風，式歌且舞，誅求之碎，所未聞命。

translations.literal: When Mi arrived, the King of Zhongshan passed the county and wished to seek fodder, hay, firewood, and kindling; Mi in a note cited the High Ancestor passing Pei, guest-ritual to old and young, mulberry-and-catalpa offerings, entirely without trouble and harassment, "I prostrate myself and consider: the enlightened king's filial thoughts take the norm, movements know prior warning, the original state looks to the wind, thus sing and dance; trifling demands of extortion—your servant has not heard the command."
translations.idiomatic: When a prince of Zhongshan demanded fodder and fuel, Mi answered with a memorandum citing Gaozu’s passage through Pei, where he honored elders and took nothing from his home villages: "Your Highness models filial conduct; your own kingdom already sings your praise—petty exactions are orders I have not received."

sentences.zh: 」自後諸王過，不敢有煩。

translations.literal: " From then on when various kings passed they did not dare have trouble.
translations.idiomatic: After that no prince dared trouble the county when passing through.

sentences.zh: 隴西王司馬子舒深敬友密，而貴勢之家憚其公直。

translations.literal: The King of Longxi Sima Zishu deeply respected and befriended Mi, while houses of noble power feared his public straightness.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zishu the Prince of Longxi esteemed Mi as a friend, while powerful families feared his impartial sternness.

sentences.zh: 密去官，為州大中正，性方直，不曲意勢位。

translations.literal: Mi left office, became Great Rectifier of the province; by nature square and straight, he did not bend intent to power and position.
translations.idiomatic: He later left office to serve as the province’s senior rectifier, upright by nature and unwilling to truckle to the mighty.

sentences.zh: 後失荀勖、張華指，左遷漢中太守，諸王多以為冤。

translations.literal: Afterward missing the finger of Xun Xu and Zhang Hua, he was shifted left to Administrator of Hanzhong; the various kings mostly thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: He fell afoul of Xun Xu and Zhang Hua and was demoted to Administrator of Hanzhong—a move many princes thought unjust.

sentences.zh: 一年去官，年六十四卒。

translations.literal: In one year he left office; at age sixty-four he died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned within a year and died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 著述理論十篇，安東將軍胡熊與皇甫士安並善之。〉

translations.literal: He wrote ten treatises on pattern-principle; General Who Pacifies the East Hu Xiong and Huangfu Shian together praised them.〉
translations.idiomatic: He left ten essays on statecraft, praised alike by Hu Xiong the Pacifier of the East and the scholar Huangfu Mi.〉

sentences.zh: 季漢輔臣贊

translations.literal: Encomia on the ministers who aided Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Encomia on the Ministers Who Served Later Han

sentences.zh: 戲以延熙四年著《季漢輔臣贊》，其所頌述，今多載於蜀書，是以記之於左。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanxi Xi composed the Encomia on the Ministers Who Aided Later Han; what it praises and narrates is now mostly carried in the Book of Shu; therefore it is recorded on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wrote the Encomia on the Ministers Who Served Later Han in Yanxi 4; most of the figures it celebrates already appear in the Book of Shu, so the text is set down here at left.

sentences.zh: 自此之後卒者，則不追諡，故或有應見稱紀而不在乎篇者也。

translations.literal: Those who died after this point were then not given posthumous titles; therefore perhaps there are some who ought to appear in praise and record but are not within the chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died afterward received no posthumous honors, so some who deserve mention never appear in these pages.

sentences.zh: 其戲之所贊而今不作傳者，餘皆注疏本末於其辭下，可以觕知其彷彿云爾。

translations.literal: Those whom Xi praised but for whom now no biography is made—for all of these I have annotated root and tip beneath his phrases, so that one may coarsely know their likeness, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: For everyone Xi praised who lacks a full biography here, I have added notes beneath his lines so the reader may grasp the outline of their lives.

sentences.zh: 昔文王歌德，武王歌興，夫命世之主，樹身行道，非唯一時，亦由開基植緒，光於來世者也。

translations.literal: In olden days King Wen sang virtue, King Wu sang rise; as for lords who command the age, establishing the body and walking the Way is not only for one time, but also because they open the foundation and plant the thread, shining on later generations.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen sang of virtue and King Wu of renewal; a true founder does not shine for one reign alone—he lays the foundations whose light reaches generations yet unborn.

sentences.zh: 自我中漢之末，王綱棄柄，雄豪並起，役殷難結，生人塗地。

translations.literal: From the end of our middle Han, the royal net cast away the handle, heroes rose together, corvée was heavy and knots were hard to untie, and the living smeared the ground.
translations.idiomatic: From the late middle Han the imperial order collapsed, warlords rose together, endless levies bound the land, and the common people were trampled like mud.

sentences.zh: 於是世主感而慮之，初自燕、代則仁聲洽著，行自齊、魯則英風播流，寄業荊、郢則臣主歸心，顧援吳、越則賢愚賴風，奮威巴、蜀則萬里肅震，厲師庸、漢則元寇斂跡，故能承高祖之始兆，复皇漢之宗祀也。

translations.literal: Thereupon the lord of the age felt and pondered it: at first from Yan and Dai then humane sound spread and showed; proceeding from Qi and Lu then heroic wind spread and flowed; lodging enterprise in Jing and Ying then minister and ruler returned hearts; turning to aid Wu and Yue then worthy and foolish relied on the wind; rousing might in Ba and Shu then within ten thousand li there was solemn shaking; sharpening troops in Yong and Han then the great bandits drew in their tracks; therefore he was able to inherit the High Ancestor's beginning omen and restore the imperial Han's ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign read the signs: from Yan and Dai his kindness spread; through Qi and Lu his heroism was known; in Jingzhou he won the hearts of lord and minister; turning to Wu and Yue he gave sage and simple alike a rallying point; his power in Ba and Shu shook the realm; his armies along the Han stilled the great rebels—thus he picked up the thread of the High Founder and restored the Han ancestral cult.

sentences.zh: 然而姦兇懟險，天徵未加，猶孟津之翔師，复須戰於鳴條也。

translations.literal: Yet the wicked and fierce were resentful and perilous; heavenly punishment had not yet been applied; it was still like the hovering host at Meng Ford—again one must battle at Mingtiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yet villainy still festered and Heaven’s axe had not fallen—it was still the host halted at Meng Ford, still a Mingtiao yet to be fought.

sentences.zh: 天祿有終，奄忽不豫。

translations.literal: Heaven's salary has an end; suddenly he was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s mandate reached its close; he fell suddenly ill.

sentences.zh: 雖攝歸一統，萬國合從者，當時俊乂扶攜翼戴，明德之所懷致也，蓋濟濟有可觀焉。

translations.literal: Although gathering returned to one unity, the ten thousand states in vertical alliance—at that time the outstanding aided, carried, winged, and bore him; it was what enlightened virtue embraced and brought; probably in great numbers there was something worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm was gathered again under one rule, it was the brilliant men of the age who lifted and shielded him—drawn by his luminous virtue—in a host well worth the telling.

sentences.zh: 遂乃並述休風，動於後聽。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they narrated the fine wind, moving later listeners.
translations.idiomatic: Here I join in recounting that fair renown for later ears.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its wording says:
translations.idiomatic: The verses run:

sentences.zh: 皇帝遺植，爰滋八方，

translations.literal: The August Emperor's remaining planting, thus nourishes the eight directions,
translations.idiomatic: The August Emperor’s seed, sown abroad, quickened life in every quarter,

sentences.zh: 別自中山，靈精是鍾，

translations.literal: Parting from Zhongshan, numinous essence is gathered here,
translations.idiomatic: Sprung from Zhongshan, where numinous essence pooled,

sentences.zh: 順期挺生，傑起龍驤。

translations.literal: Accord with the period and stand forth in birth, hero rising dragon rampant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in his destined hour, a hero rearing like a dragon in full stride.

sentences.zh: 始於燕代，伯豫君荊，

translations.literal: Beginning in Yan and Dai, lord Yu ruled Jing,
translations.idiomatic: From Yan and Dai he set out, lord of Yu and master of Jing,

sentences.zh: 吳越憑賴，望風請盟，

translations.literal: Wu and Yue relied on him, gazing at the wind and requesting alliance,
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Yue leaned on him and sued for alliance at the first rumor of his power,

sentences.zh: 挾巴跨蜀，庸漢以並。

translations.literal: Embracing Ba and straddling Shu, Yong and Han thereby combined.
translations.idiomatic: He clasped Ba and Shu and joined Yong and Han in one grip.

sentences.zh: 乾坤复秩，宗祀惟寧，

translations.literal: Heaven and earth return to order; ancestral sacrifice only is tranquil,
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth regained their order; the ancestral temple knew peace again,

sentences.zh: 躡基履跡，播德芳聲。

translations.literal: Treading the foundation, walking the traces, spreading virtue and fragrant sound.
translations.idiomatic: Following the ancient track, he spread virtue whose fragrance lingers still.

sentences.zh: 華夏思美，西伯其音，

translations.literal: Within the Xia they long for the beautiful; the Western Earl—that is his tone,
translations.idiomatic: All China recalls his grace—the Western Earl’s music lives again in him,

sentences.zh: 開慶來世，歷載攸興。

translations.literal: Opening blessing for coming generations, through years it rises.
translations.idiomatic: Opening joy for ages to come, year on year his glory grew.

sentences.zh: ──贊昭烈皇帝

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Emperor Zhaolie
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Emperor Zhaolie

sentences.zh: 忠武英高，獻策江濱，

translations.literal: Loyal and martial, heroic and high, offered strategy by the river's edge,
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and martial, towering in genius, he laid his plans beside the river,

sentences.zh: 攀吳連蜀，權我世真。

translations.literal: Climbing Wu, linking Shu, weighing our age's truth,
translations.idiomatic: He bound Wu to Shu and held the true measure of our age,

sentences.zh: 受遺阿衡，整武齊文，

translations.literal: Receiving the testament like the Yiyin, ordering arms and aligning pattern,
translations.idiomatic: He took the dying charge like Yi Yin, set war in order and brought culture to heel,

sentences.zh: 敷陳德教，理物移風，

translations.literal: Spreading and displaying virtue-teaching, ordering things and shifting wind,
translations.idiomatic: He spread moral instruction, set affairs to rights, and shifted the customs of the land,

sentences.zh: 賢愚競心，僉忘其身。

translations.literal: Worthy and foolish competed in heart; all forgot their persons.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy and simple alike gave their hearts and thought nothing of self.

sentences.zh: 誕靜邦內，四裔以綏，

translations.literal: Greatly quieting within the state, the four margins thereby pacified,
translations.idiomatic: He brought calm within the realm and peace to the four frontiers,

sentences.zh: 屢臨敵庭，實耀其威，

translations.literal: Repeatedly facing the enemy court, truly displaying his might,
translations.idiomatic: Time after time he faced the foe and flashed terror from his banners,

sentences.zh: 研精大國，恨於未夷。

translations.literal: He refined his craft against a great rival state, yet regretted that it was not yet pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the arts of statecraft against a mighty foe, and died with the north still unconquered.

sentences.zh: ──贊諸葛丞相

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Chancellor Zhuge
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Chancellor Zhuge Liang

sentences.zh: 司徒清風，是諮是臧，

translations.literal: The Minister of Education, a clear breeze—consult him, trust his judgment,
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xu, clear as a spring wind—men sought his counsel and found him true,

sentences.zh: 識愛人倫，孔音鏘鏘。

translations.literal: He knew how to cherish human relations; his noble voice rang clear.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished the bonds between men; his voice rang like polished jade.

sentences.zh: ──讚許司徒

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Minister Xu
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Minister Xu Jing

sentences.zh: 關張赳赳，出身匡世，

translations.literal: Guan and Zhang, bold and towering, came forth to rescue the age,
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Zhang rose in martial splendor to set the world aright,

sentences.zh: 扶翼攜上，雄壯虎烈。

translations.literal: They winged and bore their lord aloft, fierce as tigers in their might.
translations.idiomatic: They lifted their sovereign on their shoulders, fierce as tigers in the fray.

sentences.zh: 籓屏左右，翻飛電發，

translations.literal: They screened him left and right, darting like lightning when they struck,
translations.idiomatic: They were his shield on either hand, striking like sudden lightning,

sentences.zh: 濟於艱難，贊主洪業，

translations.literal: They brought him through hardship and aided his great enterprise,
translations.idiomatic: They carried him through peril and built the greatness of his reign,

sentences.zh: 侔跡韓耿，齊聲雙德。

translations.literal: Their deeds match Han Xin and Geng Yan; twin voices, twin virtues ring.
translations.idiomatic: Their fame stands with Han Xin and Geng Yan—two names, one measure of worth.

sentences.zh: 交待無禮，並致姦慝，

translations.literal: Their dealings with allies lacked courtesy; together they brought treachery,
translations.idiomatic: Their dealings with allies turned rash; together they courted disaster,

sentences.zh: 悼惟輕慮，隕身匡國。

translations.literal: Alas, heedless planning cost their lives in saving the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtless pride cost their lives even as they fought for the realm.

sentences.zh: ──贊關雲長、張益德

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Guan Yunchang and Zhang Yide
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei

sentences.zh: 驃騎奮起，連橫合從，

translations.literal: The Swift Cavalry rose in fury, joining vertical and horizontal alliances,
translations.idiomatic: The Swift Cavalry lord roused himself, weaving leagues east and west,

sentences.zh: 首事三秦，保據河潼。

translations.literal: He first raised arms in the Three Qins and held the Yellow River and Tong passes,
translations.idiomatic: He opened war in the Three Qins and held the Tong Gate and the Yellow River,

sentences.zh: 宗計於朝，或異或同，

translations.literal: The court debated plans—some agreed, some opposed,
translations.idiomatic: Court factions debated his strategy—some for, some against,

sentences.zh: 敵以乘釁，家破軍亡。

translations.literal: The foe seized the breach; his house was broken, his army lost.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy seized his mistake; his line was ruined, his host destroyed.

sentences.zh: 乖道反德，託鳳攀龍。

translations.literal: He turned from the Way and reversed virtue, yet sought the phoenix and climbed the dragon.
translations.idiomatic: He had strayed from the right path, yet in the end he cast his lot with the rising dragon.

sentences.zh: ──贊馬孟起

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Ma Mengqi
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Ma Chao

sentences.zh: 翼侯良謀，料世興衰，

translations.literal: The Marquis of Yi, with shrewd designs, read the age’s rise and fall,
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yi read the tides of fortune with a strategist’s cold eye,

sentences.zh: 委質於主，是訓是諮，

translations.literal: He pledged his body to his lord—his counsel, his reproof.
translations.idiomatic: He gave himself to his sovereign—to teach him and to warn him,

sentences.zh: 暫思經算，睹事知機。

translations.literal: In a moment’s thought he traced the plan; seeing events, he knew the moment.
translations.idiomatic: His mind ran the numbers in an instant; he saw each crisis coming.

sentences.zh: ──贊法孝直

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Fa Xiaozhi
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Fa Zheng

sentences.zh: 軍師美至，雅氣曄曄，

translations.literal: The Army Director, peerless in grace, his cultured air shone bright,
translations.idiomatic: The director of the army, grace incarnate, radiated quiet brilliance,

sentences.zh: 致命明主，忠情發臆，

translations.literal: He laid down his life for his enlightened lord; loyalty burst from his breast,
translations.idiomatic: He staked his life on an enlightened master; loyalty poured from his heart,

sentences.zh: 惟此義宗，亡身報德。

translations.literal: In this school of duty he forgot himself to repay kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was the very model of fealty—he spent his life repaying a debt of honor.

sentences.zh: ──贊龐士元

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Pang Shiyuan
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Pang Tong

sentences.zh: 將軍敦壯，摧峰登難，

translations.literal: The general, staunch and mighty, stormed the heights through peril,
translations.idiomatic: The general, solid as a fortress, broke enemy lines on the hardest ground,

sentences.zh: 立功立事，於時之幹。

translations.literal: He founded deeds and deeds became renown—the backbone of his age.
translations.idiomatic: He built achievement on achievement—the mainstay of his generation.

sentences.zh: ──贊黃漢昇

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Huang Hansheng
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Huang Zhong

sentences.zh: 掌軍清節，亢然恆常，

translations.literal: He held the army with pure integrity, upright and ever constant,
translations.idiomatic: He commanded with spotless honor, steady as a plumb line,

sentences.zh: 讜言惟司，民思其綱。

translations.literal: Frank counsel was his charge; the people longed for his rule.
translations.idiomatic: Candor was his office; the people looked to him as their standard.

sentences.zh: ──贊董幼宰

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Dong Youzai
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Dong He

sentences.zh: 安遠強志，允休允烈，

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the Far, strong in resolve, both mild and fierce,
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifier of the Far, iron in will, yet capable of mercy and of fire,

sentences.zh: 輕財果壯，當難不惑，

translations.literal: He scorned wealth, was bold and stout; faced crisis without doubt,
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for gold, struck hard and fast, and never flinched in danger,

sentences.zh: 以少禦多，殊方保業。

translations.literal: With few he mastered many and kept his charge in distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: He held a distant frontier with a handful against a host.

sentences.zh: ──贊鄧孔山

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Deng Kongshan
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Deng Fang

sentences.zh: 孔山名方，南郡人也。

translations.literal: Kongshan’s given name was Fang; he was a man of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Fang, style Kongshan, came from Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 以荊州從事隨先主入蜀。

translations.literal: As a staff member of Jingzhou he followed the First Sovereign into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Shu as an aide on the Jingzhou staff.

sentences.zh: 蜀既定，為犍為屬國都尉，因易郡名，為硃提太守，選為安遠將軍、庲降都督，住南昌縣。

translations.literal: When Shu was settled he became Commandant of the Dependent State of Qianwei; thereupon the commandery name was changed and he became Administrator of Zhuti; he was selected General Who Pacifies the Far and Area Commander of Laixiang, stationed at Nanchang county.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest he was named commandant of the Qianwei dependent state, then Administrator of the renamed Zhuti command, then General Who Pacifies the Far and area commander at Laixiang, with his seat at Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 章武二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhangwu 2.

sentences.zh: 失其行事，故不為傳。

translations.literal: His deeds are lost; therefore no biography is made.
translations.idiomatic: His career is no longer recorded, so no full biography is given.

sentences.zh: 揚威才幹，欷歔文武，

translations.literal: The General Who Spreads Might, talented and capable, sighing over civil and martial arts,
translations.idiomatic: The Spreader of Might, gifted in both civil and military affairs,

sentences.zh: 當官理任，衎衎辯舉，

translations.literal: In office he ordered duty; his eloquence rose clear and steady.
