translations.idiomatic: He ran his office with poise; his arguments rang clear and measured,

sentences.zh: 圖殖財施，有義有敘。

translations.literal: He plotted to grow wealth and give alms—both duty and order.
translations.idiomatic: He grew rich only to give it away—with principle and good order.

sentences.zh: ──贊費賓伯

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Fei Binbo
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Fei Guan

sentences.zh: 賓伯名觀，江夏鄳人也。

translations.literal: Binbo’s given name was Guan; he was a man of Mao in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Guan, style Binbo, was a native of Mao in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 劉璋母，觀之族姑，璋又以女妻觀。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang’s mother was Guan’s clan aunt; Zhang also gave a daughter to Guan as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang’s mother was Guan’s aunt by clan, and Zhang married a daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 觀建安十八年參李嚴軍，拒先主於綿竹，與嚴俱降，先主既定益州，拜為裨將軍，後為巴郡太守、江州都督，建興元年封都亭侯，加振威將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jian’an Guan joined Li Yan’s army, resisted the First Sovereign at Mianzhu, and with Yan both surrendered; when the First Sovereign had settled Yizhou he was appointed Lieutenant General, later became Administrator of Ba command and Area Commander of Jiangzhou; in the first year of Jianxing he was enfeoffed village marquis at the metropolitan pavilion and additionally titled General Who Spreads Might.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an 18 he served under Li Yan against the First Sovereign at Mianzhu, surrendered with Yan, and after Yizhou fell was made lieutenant general, later Ba’s administrator and Jiangzhou area commander; in Jianxing 1 he received a village marquisate at the pavilion and the title General Who Spreads Might.

sentences.zh: 觀為人善於交接。

translations.literal: Guan as a person was skilled in social dealings.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was a master of personal relations.

sentences.zh: 都護李嚴性自矜高，護軍輔匡等年位與嚴相次，而嚴不與親褻；

translations.literal: Director of Retainers Li Yan by nature was proud and lofty; Protector Fu Kuang and others matched him in age and rank, yet Yan would not become intimate with them;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan the director of retainers was arrogant by nature; Fu Kuang and other officers of similar age and rank could not win his intimacy;

sentences.zh: 觀年少嚴二十餘歲，而與嚴通狎如時輩雲。

translations.literal: Guan was more than twenty years younger than Yan, yet with Yan he was on familiar terms like men of the same generation, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: yet Guan, though more than twenty years his junior, moved in Yan’s circle as an equal.

sentences.zh: 年三十七卒。

translations.literal: He died at age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 失其行事，故不為傳。

translations.literal: His deeds are lost; therefore no biography is made.
translations.idiomatic: His career is no longer recorded, so no full biography is given.

sentences.zh: 屯騎主舊，固節不移，

translations.literal: The Colonel of Garrison Cavalry upheld old ties; his integrity never shifted,
translations.idiomatic: The garrison cavalry colonel clung to old loyalties and never bent his honor,

sentences.zh: 既就初命，盡心世規，

translations.literal: Once he accepted his first charge, he gave his heart to the age’s norms,
translations.idiomatic: From his first appointment he gave his whole heart to public duty,

sentences.zh: 軍資所恃，是辨是裨。

translations.literal: On what the army relied he was both clear-eyed and helpful.
translations.idiomatic: The host leaned on him for supplies—for clarity and steady support.

sentences.zh: ──贊王文儀

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Wang Wenyi
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Wang Lian

sentences.zh: 尚書清尚，敕行整身，

translations.literal: The Minister, pure in aspiration, ordered his conduct and set his person aright,
translations.idiomatic: The minister, austere in purpose, disciplined himself before others,

sentences.zh: 抗志存義，味覽典文，

translations.literal: He held high purpose and kept to duty; he savored the classics’ text,
translations.idiomatic: He nursed a high purpose and loved the taste of canonical learning,

sentences.zh: 倚其高風，好侔古人。

translations.literal: He leaned on lofty airs and loved to match the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: He walked in the wind of the ancients and strove to match their example.

sentences.zh: ──贊劉子初

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Liu Zichu
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Liu Ba

sentences.zh: 安漢雍容，或婚或賓，

translations.literal: The Marquis Who Pacifies Han, easy in manner—now kin, now guest,
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifier of Han, gracious in bearing—kinsman to some, guest to others,

sentences.zh: 見禮當時，是謂循臣。

translations.literal: Honored in his own day, he was called a model minister.
translations.idiomatic: Honored in his time, he was reckoned a model servant of the throne.

sentences.zh: ──贊麋子仲

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Mi Zizhong
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Mi Zhu

sentences.zh: 少府修慎，鴻臚明真，

translations.literal: The Minister of the Lesser Treasury, careful and prudent; the Grand Herald, bright and true,
translations.idiomatic: The minister of the lesser treasury, scrupulous; the grand herald, lucid and just,

sentences.zh: 諫議隱行，儒林天文。

translations.literal: The remonstrator’s hidden ways; the forest of scholars and heaven’s patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrator in quiet service; masters of the classics and of the stars.

sentences.zh: 宣班大化，或首或林。

translations.literal: They spread the great transformation—some at the fore, some in the grove.
translations.idiomatic: They spread the king’s transforming power—some in the van, some in the ranks.

sentences.zh: ──贊王元泰、何彥英、杜輔國、周仲直

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Wang Yuantai, He Yanning, Du Fuguo, and Zhou Zhongzhi
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Wang Mou, He Zong, Du Qiong, and Zhou Shu

sentences.zh: 王元泰名謀，漢嘉人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yuantai’s given name was Mou; he was a man of Hanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mou, style Yuantai, came from Hanjia.

sentences.zh: 有容止操行。

translations.literal: He had bearing and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He carried himself with dignity.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時，為巴郡太守，還為州治中從事。

translations.literal: Under Liu Zhang he was Administrator of Ba command, then returned to become provincial Adjunct Clerk for the Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he governed Ba, then became the provincial headquarters adjutant.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，領牧，以為別駕。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign settled Yizhou and held the shepherdcy, he made him Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Sovereign took Yizhou he named him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 先主為漢中王，用荊楚宿士零陵賴恭為太常，南陽黃柱為光祿勳，謀為少府；

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign became King of Hanzhong, he used the seasoned Jing-Chu gentleman Lai Gong of Lingling as Minister of Ceremonies, Huang Zhu of Nanyang as Superintendant of the Household, and Mou as Minister of the Lesser Treasury;
translations.idiomatic: When the First Sovereign became king of Hanzhong he appointed Lai Gong of Lingling Minister of Ceremonies, Huang Zhu of Nanyang superintendant of the household, and Wang Mou minister of the lesser treasury;

sentences.zh: 建興初，賜爵關內侯，後代賴恭為太常。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianxing he was granted noble rank as village marquis within the passes, afterward replaced Lai Gong as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianxing he received a village marquisate inside the passes and later succeeded Lai Gong as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 恭、柱、謀皆失其行事，故不為傳。

translations.literal: Gong, Zhu, and Mou—all lost their deeds; therefore no biography is made.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Gong, Huang Zhu, and Wang Mou left too slight a record for separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 恭子厷，為丞相西曹令史，隨諸葛亮於漢中，早夭，亮甚惜之，與留府長史參軍張裔、蔣琬書曰：「令史失賴厷，掾屬喪楊顒，為朝中損益多矣。

translations.literal: Gong’s son Hong was West Bureau clerk to the Chancellor and followed Zhuge Liang in Hanzhong; he died young, and Liang greatly grieved him. In a letter to Chief Clerk Zhang Yi and Jiang Wan, who remained at headquarters, he said: "The clerk’s office has lost Lai Hong, the staff has lost Yang Yong—for the court the loss is great."
translations.idiomatic: Lai Gong’s son Hong served as Zhuge Liang’s west-bureau clerk in Hanzhong and died young; Liang mourned him deeply and wrote to Zhang Yi and Jiang Wan at headquarters, "We have lost Lai Hong from the clerk’s office and Yang Yong from the staff—the damage to the administration is heavy."

sentences.zh: 」顒亦荊州人也。

translations.literal: " Yong was also a man of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yong was likewise from Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後大將軍蔣琬問張休曰：「漢嘉前輩有王元泰，今誰繼者？

translations.literal: Afterward Grand General Jiang Wan asked Zhang Xiu: "Among the elders of Hanjia there was Wang Yuantai—who succeeds him now?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand General Jiang Wan asked Zhang Xiu, "Hanjia once had Wang Yuantai—who carries that tradition today?"

sentences.zh: 」休對曰：「至於元泰，州里無繼，況鄙郡乎！

translations.literal: " Xiu replied: "As for Yuantai, there is no successor in the province—how much less in this humble commandery!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu answered, "After Yuantai there is no one of that stature even in the province—let alone in our poor commandery."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " Thus was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard he commanded.

sentences.zh: 〈《襄陽記》曰：楊顒字子昭，楊儀宗人也。

translations.literal: The Xiangyang Ji says: Yang Yong, courtesy name Zizhao, was a clansman of Yang Yi in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang Ji records Yang Yong, courtesy Zizhao, a kinsman of Yang Yi from Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入蜀，為巴郡太守，丞相諸葛亮主簿。

translations.literal: He entered Shu, became Administrator of Ba command, and chief clerk to Chancellor Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He came to Shu as Administrator of Ba and chief clerk to Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮嘗自校簿書，顒直入諫曰：「為治有體，上下不可相侵，請為明公以作家譬之。

translations.literal: Liang once personally checked the account books; Yong went straight in and remonstrated, saying: "There is a proper body to government; superiors and inferiors must not encroach on one another. Allow your servant to explain by the analogy of a household.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Liang was personally auditing the ledgers, Yong walked in unannounced and said, "Government has its proper form—superiors must not do underlings’ work. Permit me to compare it to running a household.

sentences.zh: 今有人使奴執耕稼，婢典炊爨，雞主司晨，犬主吠盜，牛負重載，馬涉遠路，私業無曠，所求皆足，雍容高枕，飲食而已，忽一旦盡欲以身親其役，不復付任，勞其體力，為此碎務，形疲神困，終無一成。

translations.literal: Suppose a man has slaves plow the fields, maids tend the cooking, the cock keep dawn, the dog bark at thieves, the ox bear heavy loads, and the horse travel far roads—private business never idle, every need supplied—so he can lounge at ease with pillow high and only eat and drink; then suddenly one morning he insists on doing every task himself, hands over nothing, tires body and strength in these petty chores, until body wearies and spirit fails, and in the end nothing is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Imagine a master who lets slaves till the soil, maids mind the kitchen, cocks herald dawn, dogs warn off thieves, oxen haul loads, and horses bear him on long roads—so his estate runs itself while he rests—then one day he insists on doing every chore himself, wears himself out on trifles, and accomplishes nothing.

sentences.zh: 豈其智之不如奴婢雞狗哉？

translations.literal: Could it be that his intelligence falls short of slaves, maids, cocks, and dogs?
translations.idiomatic: Is he less wise than a slave, a maid, a rooster, or a hound?

sentences.zh: 失為家主之法也。

translations.literal: He has lost the method of being master of a household.
translations.idiomatic: He has forgotten how to be master of his own house.

sentences.zh: 是故古人稱坐而論道謂之三公，作而行之謂之士大夫。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients called those who sit and discuss the Way the three dukes, and those who act and carry it out the grandees and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said the three dukes sit to discuss the Way, while ministers rise to execute it.

sentences.zh: 故邴吉不問橫道死人而憂牛喘，陳平不肯知錢穀之數，云自有主者，彼誠達於位分之體也。

translations.literal: Thus Bing Ji did not ask about corpses in the crossroads but worried over the panting of oxen; Chen Ping refused to know the numbers of cash and grain, saying there were officials in charge—those men truly grasped the substance of office and duty.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji ignored corpses in the road but fretted over a panting ox; Chen Ping refused to memorize revenue figures, saying specialists existed for that—both understood the limits of high office.

sentences.zh: 今明公為治，乃躬自校簿書，流汗竟日，不亦勞乎！

translations.literal: Now, my lord, in governing you personally examine account books, sweat all day—is it not laborious!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you, my lord, pore over every ledger until you sweat through the day—is that not wasted labor?"

sentences.zh: 」亮謝之。

translations.literal: " Liang apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang thanked him for the rebuke.

sentences.zh: 後為東曹屬典選舉。

translations.literal: Afterward he became a member of the Eastern Bureau in charge of selections.
translations.idiomatic: Yong later joined the eastern bureau and supervised appointments.

sentences.zh: 顒死，亮垂泣三日。〉

translations.literal: When Yong died, Liang wept for three days.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Yong died, Liang mourned him for three full days.〉

sentences.zh: 何彥英名宗，蜀郡郫人也。

translations.literal: He Yanning’s given name was Zong; he was a man of Pi in Shujun.
translations.idiomatic: He Zong, style Yanning, came from Pi in Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 事廣漢任安學，精究安術，與杜瓊同師而名問過之。

translations.literal: He studied under Ren An of Guanghan, thoroughly investigated An’s arts, and had the same teacher as Du Qiong but his fame and reputation surpassed Qiong’s.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Ren An of Guanghan, mastered Ren’s methods, and outshone his fellow student Du Qiong.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時，為犍為太守。

translations.literal: Under Liu Zhang he was Administrator of Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he served as Administrator of Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，領牧，闢為從事祭酒。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign settled Yizhou and held the shepherdcy, he summoned him as Libationer Adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Sovereign took Yizhou he called him to serve as libationer-adjunct.

sentences.zh: 後援引圖、讖，勸先主即尊號。

translations.literal: Afterward citing charts and prophecies, he urged the First Sovereign to assume the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: He later cited charts and apocrypha to urge the First Sovereign to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 踐阼之後，遷為大鴻臚。

translations.literal: After the ascension he was moved up to Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: After the enthronement he was promoted to grand herald.

sentences.zh: 建興中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Jianxing era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Jianxing years.

sentences.zh: 失其行事，故不為傳。

translations.literal: His deeds are lost; therefore no biography is made.
translations.idiomatic: His career is no longer recorded, so no full biography is given.

sentences.zh: 子雙，字漢偶。

translations.literal: His son Shuang, courtesy name Han'ou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuang bore the courtesy name Han’ou.

sentences.zh: 滑稽談笑，有淳于髡、東方朔之風。

translations.literal: He was witty in jest and talk, having the air of Chunyu Kun and Dongfang Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: He had the quick wit and jesting manner of a Chunyu Kun or Dongfang Shuo.

sentences.zh: 為雙柏長。

translations.literal: He became magistrate of Shuangbai.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Shuangbai.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 車騎高勁，惟其汎愛，

translations.literal: The General of Chariots and Cavalry, lofty and firm, only his broad love,
translations.idiomatic: The general of chariots and cavalry, stern and high-minded, generous to all,

sentences.zh: 以弱制強，不陷危墜。

translations.literal: With weakness controlling strength, he did not fall into peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He turned weakness to strength and never fell into ruin.

sentences.zh: ──贊吳子遠

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Wu Ziyuan
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Wu Yi

sentences.zh: 壹族弟班，字元雄，大將軍何進官屬吳匡之子也。

translations.literal: Yi’s younger clan cousin Ban, courtesy name Yuanxiong, was the son of Wu Kuang, who had served under Grand General He Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ban, courtesy Yuanxiong, was Wu Yi’s younger clansman and the son of Wu Kuang, an officer under Grand General He Jin.

sentences.zh: 以豪俠稱，官位常與壹相亞。

translations.literal: He was famed as a knight-errant; his offices were always next after Yi’s.
translations.idiomatic: He had a swashbuckling reputation and usually ranked just below Wu Yi.

sentences.zh: 先主時，為領軍。

translations.literal: In the First Sovereign’s time he was Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the First Sovereign he commanded the central army.

sentences.zh: 後主世，稍遷至驃騎將軍，假節，封綿竹侯。

translations.literal: In the Later Lord’s age he was gradually moved up to General of Agile Cavalry, granted the staff of authority, and enfeoffed marquis of Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Lord he rose to General of Agile Cavalry with the credential staff and a marquisate at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 安漢宰南，奮擊舊鄉，

translations.literal: The Marquis Who Pacifies Han ruled the south, striking hard in his old home,
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifier of Han governed the south and smote his native region,

sentences.zh: 翦除蕪穢，惟刑以張，

translations.literal: He cut away rank growth; only punishments spread his rule,
translations.idiomatic: He cleared away the chaff and let the law speak for itself,

sentences.zh: 廣遷蠻濮，國用用強。

translations.literal: He broadly moved Man and Pu; the state’s use thereby grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled Man and Pu tribes until the treasury grew strong again.

sentences.zh: ──贊李德昂

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Li De'ang
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Li Hui

sentences.zh: 輔漢惟聰，既機且惠，

translations.literal: He aided Han with keen hearing—both alert and kind,
translations.idiomatic: He served Shu with a sharp ear—perceptive and humane,

sentences.zh: 因言遠思，切問近對，

translations.literal: Through words he thought far; pressing questions met answers near at hand,
translations.idiomatic: His words reached far; hard questions found plain answers at hand,

sentences.zh: 贊時休美，和我業世。

translations.literal: He praised the age’s good and beautiful, harmonizing our enterprise through generations.
translations.idiomatic: He praised the good in his time and steadied the work of generations.

sentences.zh: ──贊張君嗣

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Zhang Juesi
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Zhang Yi

sentences.zh: 鎮北敏思，籌畫有方，

translations.literal: The General Who Guards the North, keen in thought, planned with method,
translations.idiomatic: The northern guardian, quick of mind, laid plans that always fit the case,

sentences.zh: 導師禳穢，遂事成章。

translations.literal: He guided the host and averted foulness; when the deed was done it took proper form.
translations.idiomatic: He led the army and cleared away rot until every task fell into place.

sentences.zh: 偏任東隅，末命不祥，

translations.literal: Solely entrusted with the eastern corner, his final fate was ill-omened,
translations.idiomatic: Left alone on the eastern flank, his last orders brought no blessing,

sentences.zh: 哀悲本志，放流殊疆。

translations.literal: Grief for his original intent; cast out to a distant border.
translations.idiomatic: Men mourned the aim he began with—exiled to a distant frontier.

sentences.zh: ──贊黃公衡

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Huang Gongheng
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Huang Quan

sentences.zh: 越騎惟忠，厲志自祗，

translations.literal: The Colonel of Agile Cavalry was only loyal; he sharpened his will and guarded himself,
translations.idiomatic: The agile-cavalry colonel was all devotion—he schooled his will and kept his own counsel,

sentences.zh: 職於內外，念公忘私。

translations.literal: His duties lay within and without; he thought of the public and forgot private interest.
translations.idiomatic: He served inside the court and out, minding the state before himself.

sentences.zh: ──贊楊季休

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Yang Jixiu
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Yang Hong

sentences.zh: 征南厚重，征西忠克，

translations.literal: The south-conquering general was staunch; the west-conquering general loyal and able,
translations.idiomatic: The southern conqueror was weighty; the western conqueror loyal and capable,

sentences.zh: 統時選士，猛將之烈。

translations.literal: They directed the age and chose men; fierce generals in their fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: They picked the men of the hour—fierce captains who lived up to the name.

sentences.zh: ──贊趙子龍、陳叔至

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Zhao Zilong and Chen Shuzhi
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Zhao Yun and Chen Dao

sentences.zh: 叔至名到，汝南人也。

translations.literal: Shuzhi’s given name was Dao; he was a man of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dao, style Shuzhi, came from Runan.

sentences.zh: 自豫州隨先主，名位常亞趙雲，俱以忠勇稱。

translations.literal: From Yuzhou he followed the First Sovereign; his fame and rank were always next after Zhao Yun, and both were famed for loyalty and courage.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the First Sovereign from Yuzhou, ranked just below Zhao Yun, and both were known for loyalty and valor.

sentences.zh: 建興初，官至永安都督、征西將軍，封亭侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianxing his office reached Area Commander of Yong'an, General Who Conquers the West, and enfeoffment as village marquis at the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianxing he became Yong’an area commander, General Who Conquers the West, and a village marquis at the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 鎮南粗強，監軍尚篤，

translations.literal: The General Who Guards the South was rough and strong; the army supervisor still earnest,
translations.idiomatic: The southern guardian was blunt and tough; the army supervisor still steadfast,

sentences.zh: 並豫戎任，任自封裔。

translations.literal: Both took part in military duty; their offices rose from their own descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Both bore arms for the state; their sons inherited their posts.

sentences.zh: ──贊輔元弼、劉南和

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Fu Yuanbi and Liu Nanhe
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Fu Kuang and Liu Yong

sentences.zh: 輔元弼名匡，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Fu Yuanbi’s given name was Kuang; he was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Kuang, style Yuanbi, was a native of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 隨先主入蜀。

translations.literal: He followed the First Sovereign into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He marched into Shu in the First Sovereign’s train.

sentences.zh: 益州既定，為巴郡太守。

translations.literal: When Yizhou was settled he became Administrator of Ba command.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhou fell he became Administrator of Ba.

sentences.zh: 建興中，徙鎮南，為右將軍，封中鄉侯。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing era he was transferred to General Who Guards the South, became General of the Right, and enfeoffed marquis of Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianxing he was shifted to General Who Guards the South, promoted to general of the right, and ennobled as marquis of Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 劉南和名邕，義陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Nanhe’s given name was Yong; he was a man of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong, style Nanhe, came from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 隨先主入蜀。

translations.literal: He followed the First Sovereign into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He too crossed into Shu with the First Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 益州既定，為江陽太守。

translations.literal: When Yizhou was settled he became Administrator of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhou fell he governed Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 建興中，稍遷至監軍後將軍，賜爵關內侯，卒。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing era he was gradually moved up to Rear General Supervisor of the Army, was granted noble rank as village marquis within the passes, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing he rose to rear general and army supervisor, received a village marquisate inside the passes, and died.

sentences.zh: 子式嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 少子武，有文，與樊建齊名，官亦至尚書。

translations.literal: His younger son Wu had literary talent, was equally famed with Fan Jian, and his office also reached Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Wu was a scholar of note, ranked with Fan Jian, and rose to minister.

sentences.zh: 司農性才，敷述允章，

translations.literal: The Minister of Agriculture, talented by nature, set forth patterns that were true and bright,
translations.idiomatic: The minister of agriculture, gifted in letters, framed clear and fitting arguments,

sentences.zh: 藻麗辭理，斐斐有光。

translations.literal: His phrases were ornate, his reasoning clear; they shone with luster.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was ornate, his logic lucid, and it glowed with polish.

sentences.zh: ──贊秦子敕

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Qin Zichi
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Qin Mi

sentences.zh: 正方受遺，豫聞後綱，

translations.literal: Zhengfang received the testament and foreknew the later framework,
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan took the dying charge and foresaw the shape of things to come,

sentences.zh: 不陳不僉，造此異端，

translations.literal: Neither remonstrated nor concurred; he opened this aberrant course,
translations.idiomatic: Yet he neither advised nor assented—he opened this crooked path,

sentences.zh: 斥逐當時，任業以喪。

translations.literal: Was driven off in his own day; undertaking office, he thereby lost it.
translations.idiomatic: Was cast out in his lifetime and threw his career away.

sentences.zh: ──贊李正方

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Li Zhengfang
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Li Yan

sentences.zh: 文長剛粗，臨難受命，

translations.literal: Wenchang was brash and rough; facing peril he received orders,
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan was blunt and rough; in crisis he took the command,

sentences.zh: 折衝外禦，鎮保國境。

translations.literal: He broke enemy fronts abroad and guarded the state’s borders.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered foes on the frontier and held the marches secure.

sentences.zh: 不協不和，忘節言亂，

translations.literal: Not concordant, not harmonious; forgetting integrity, his words turned chaotic,
translations.idiomatic: He could not work with others; he forgot loyalty and his tongue ran wild,

sentences.zh: 疾終惜始，實惟厥性。

translations.literal: Hastening to the end, pity the beginning—such truly was his nature.
translations.idiomatic: His end invites pity when one thinks how he began—that was his nature.

sentences.zh: ──贊魏文長

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Wei Wenchang
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Wei Yan

sentences.zh: 威公狷狹，取異眾人；

translations.literal: Lord Wei was narrow and constrained, taking himself apart from the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei was stiff-necked and set himself apart from other men;

sentences.zh: 閒則及理，逼則傷侵，

translations.literal: At leisure he reached principle; under pressure he harmed and encroached,
translations.idiomatic: At ease he could be reasonable; under pressure he turned cutting and cruel,

sentences.zh: 舍順入兇，大易之雲。

translations.literal: Leaving the compliant he entered the vicious—so speaks the Great Change.
translations.idiomatic: He left the straight road for violence—as the Classic of Change warns.

sentences.zh: ──贊楊威公

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Yang Weigong
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Yang Yi

sentences.zh: 季常良實，文經勤類，

translations.literal: Jichang was good and solid; Wenjing diligent in kind;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang was steady and true; Wei Jiong diligent in his class;

sentences.zh: 士元言規，處仁聞計，

translations.literal: Shiyuan spoke counsel; Churen was famed for plans;
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji offered maxims; Zhang Cun was known for strategy;

sentences.zh: 孔休文祥，或才或臧，

translations.literal: Kongxiu and Wenxiang—some talented, some good;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guan and Xi Zhen—each gifted or worthy in his way;

sentences.zh: 播播述志，楚之蘭芳。

translations.literal: They broadcast their aims; orchid fragrance of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: They set forth their ideals—the orchid scent of old Chu.

sentences.zh: ──贊馬季常、衛文經、韓士元、張處仁、殷孔休、習文祥

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Ma Jichang, Wei Wenjing, Han Shiyuan, Zhang Churen, Yin Kongxiu, and Xi Wenxiang
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Ma Liang, Wei Jiong, Han Ji, Zhang Cun, Yin Guan, and Xi Zhen

sentences.zh: 文經、士元，皆失其名實、行事、郡縣。

translations.literal: Wenjing and Shiyuan—both have lost their true names, deeds, and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiong and Han Ji— their full names, careers, and home counties are no longer known.

sentences.zh: 處仁本名存，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Churen’s original given name was Cun; he was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cun was originally named Cun and came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 以荊州從事隨先主入蜀，南次至雒，以為廣漢太守。

translations.literal: As a staff member of Jingzhou he followed the First Sovereign into Shu, halted southward at Luo, and was made Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Shu on the Jingzhou staff, paused the advance at Luo, and was named Administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 存素不服龐統，統中矢卒，先主發言嘉嘆，存曰：「統雖盡忠可惜，然違大雅之義。

translations.literal: Cun had never submitted to Pang Tong; when Tong was hit by an arrow and died, the First Sovereign spoke words of praise and sighing, and Cun said: "Though Tong exhausted loyalty it is regrettable, yet he violated the meaning of the great standard."
translations.idiomatic: Cun had never respected Pang Tong; when Tong fell to an arrow the First Sovereign praised him, but Cun said, "Tong was loyal, yes, but he fell short of the great norm."

sentences.zh: 」先主怒曰：「統殺身成仁，更為非也？

translations.literal: The First Sovereign angrily said: "Tong destroyed his body to achieve humaneness—do you call that wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: The First Sovereign retorted, "Tong gave his life for duty—how can you call that wrong?"

sentences.zh: 」免存官。

translations.literal: He dismissed Cun from office.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Cun of his post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，病卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 失其行事，故不為傳。

translations.literal: His deeds are lost; therefore no biography is made.
translations.idiomatic: His career is no longer recorded, so no full biography is given.

sentences.zh: 孔休名觀，為荊州主簿別駕從事，見《先主傳》。

translations.literal: Kongxiu’s given name was Guan; he was Chief Clerk and Chief Clerk for Separate Carriage of Jingzhou—see the Biography of the First Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guan, style Kongxiu, served Jingzhou as chief clerk and separate-carriage chief clerk—see the First Sovereign’s biography.

sentences.zh: 失其郡縣。

translations.literal: His commandery is lost.
translations.idiomatic: His home commandery is no longer recorded.

sentences.zh: 文祥名禎，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Wenxiang’s given name was Zhen; he was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zhen, style Wenxiang, was a native of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 隨先主入蜀，歷雒、郫令，

translations.literal: He followed the First Sovereign into Shu and successively was magistrate of Luo and Pi,
translations.idiomatic: He followed the First Sovereign into Shu and served as magistrate of Luo and Pi,

translations.literal: Parenthetical: nan (“south”).
translations.idiomatic: Editorial gloss: the text supplies nan, yielding Nanchong, before the following title “Administrator of Guanghan.”

sentences.zh: 廣漢太守。

translations.literal: Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 失其行事。

translations.literal: His deeds are lost.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of his career is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 子忠，官至尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhong reached Gentleman of the Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong rose to gentleman in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 〈《襄陽記》曰：習禎有風流，善談論，名亞龐統，而在馬良之右。

translations.literal: The Xiangyang Ji says: Xi Zhen had polish and grace, was skilled in discourse; his fame was next after Pang Tong but above Ma Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang Ji says Xi Zhen was elegant and eloquent—second only to Pang Tong, ranked above Ma Liang.

sentences.zh: 子忠，亦有名。

translations.literal: His son Zhong also had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong likewise won a name.

sentences.zh: 忠子隆，為步兵校尉，掌校秘書。〉

translations.literal: Zhong’s son Long was Colonel of Foot Soldiers and supervised collation of the secretariat archives.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhong’s son Long became colonel of foot soldiers and oversaw the palace library archives.〉

sentences.zh: 國山休風，永南耽思；

translations.literal: Guoshan, a fine breeze; Yongnan sunk in thought;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo—clear as a breeze; Li Nan—lost in reflection;

sentences.zh: 盛衡、承伯，言藏言時；

translations.literal: Shengheng, Chengbo—words stored, words timely;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun, Ma Qi—speech held back or spoken to the hour;

sentences.zh: 孫德果銳，偉南篤常；

translations.literal: Sun De keen and sharp; Weinan earnest and constant;
translations.idiomatic: Li Sun—sharp and bold; Li Wei—steady and true;

sentences.zh: 德緒、義強，志壯氣剛。

translations.literal: Dexu and Yiqiang—ambitions bold, temperaments hard.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Lu and Wang Yi—high mettle and iron nerve.

sentences.zh: 濟濟脩志，蜀之芬香。

translations.literal: In thronging numbers they refined their aims—Shu’s sweet fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: So many, each honing his purpose—the perfume of Shu.

sentences.zh: ──贊王國山、李永南、馬盛衡、馬承伯、李孫德、李偉南，龔德緒、王義強

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Wang Guoshan, Li Yongnan, Ma Shengheng, Ma Chengbo, Li Sunde, Li Weinan, Gong Dexu, and Wang Yiqiang
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Wang Guo, Li Shao, Ma Xun, Ma Qi, Li Fu, Li Wei, Gong Lu, and Wang Yi

sentences.zh: 國山名甫，廣漢郪人也。

translations.literal: Guoshan’s given name was Fu; he was a man of Qi in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo, style Guoshan, came from Qi in Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 好人流言議。

translations.literal: He loved to circulate gossip and discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He loved rumor and debate.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時，為州書佐。

translations.literal: Under Liu Zhang he was provincial clerical aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he served as a provincial clerk.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀後，為綿竹令，還為荊州議曹從事。

translations.literal: After the First Sovereign settled Shu he became magistrate of Mianzhu, then returned to be Consulting Clerk Adjunct of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he was magistrate of Mianzhu, then consulting clerk on the Jingzhou staff.

sentences.zh: 隨先主徵吳，軍敗於秭歸，遇害。

translations.literal: He followed the First Sovereign on the campaign against Wu; the army was defeated at Zigui and he met death.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with the First Sovereign against Wu and died when the army was routed at Zigui.

sentences.zh: 子祐，有父風，官至尚書右選郎。

translations.literal: His son You had his father’s manner and reached Gentleman of the Right Selection Bureau among the Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His son You took after him and rose to gentleman of the right selection bureau.

sentences.zh: 盛衡名勳，承伯名齊，皆巴西閬中人也。

translations.literal: Shengheng’s given name was Xun; Chengbo’s given name was Qi; both were men of Langzhong in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun and Ma Qi, styles Shengheng and Chengbo, were brothers from Langzhong in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 勳，劉璋時為州書佐，先主定蜀，闢為左將軍屬，後轉州別駕從事，卒。

translations.literal: Xun, under Liu Zhang was provincial clerical aide; when the First Sovereign settled Shu he was summoned as staff to the General of the Left, afterward was transferred to provincial Adjunct Clerk for Separate Carriage, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun had been a provincial clerk under Liu Zhang; after Liu Bei took Shu he joined the left general’s staff, later became the province’s chief clerk, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 齊為太守張飛功曹。

translations.literal: Qi was merit officer under Administrator Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qi served as Zhang Fei’s merit officer when Fei was administrator.

sentences.zh: 飛貢之先主，為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Fei presented him to the First Sovereign, and he became Gentleman of the Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Fei recommended him to the First Sovereign, who named him a gentleman in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 建興中，從事丞相掾，遷廣漢太守，復為

translations.literal: In the Jianxing era he served as clerk under the Chancellor, was moved up to Administrator of Guanghan, and again became
translations.idiomatic: During Jianxing he worked as a chancellor’s clerk, was promoted to Administrator of Guanghan, and was then appointed

translations.literal: Parenthetical: fei (“Fei”).
translations.idiomatic: Editorial gloss: read Fei, for Zhang Fei, before the title “army advisor.”

sentences.zh: 參軍。

translations.literal: army advisor.
translations.idiomatic: army adviser on Zhang Fei’s staff.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，為尚書。

translations.literal: When Liang died he became Minister.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang’s death he entered the ministry as a full minister.

sentences.zh: 勳、齊皆以才幹自顯見；

translations.literal: Xun and Qi both by talent and capacity displayed themselves conspicuously;
translations.idiomatic: Both Ma brothers won fame for their administrative gifts;

sentences.zh: 歸信於州黨，不如姚伷。

translations.literal: in returning trust among the provincial clique they did not match Yao Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: yet neither enjoyed the hometown confidence that Yao Zhou commanded.

sentences.zh: 孫德名福，梓潼涪人也。

translations.literal: Sun De’s given name was Fu; he was a man of Fu in Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, style Sunde, came from Fu in Zitong commandery.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州後，為書佐、西充國長、成都令。

translations.literal: After the First Sovereign settled Yizhou he was clerical aide, magistrate of Western Chongguo, and magistrate of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhou fell he served as clerk, magistrate of Western Chongguo, and then of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 建興元年，徙巴西太守，為江州督、楊威將軍，入為尚書僕射，封平陽亭侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he was transferred to Administrator of Ba command, became supervisor of Jiangzhou and General Who Displays Might, entered as Vice Minister Secretary, and was enfeoffed village marquis of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 he became Administrator of Ba, Jiangzhou supervisor, and General Who Displays Might, then vice minister of the secretariat with a village marquisate at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 延熙初，大將軍蔣琬出征漢中，福以前監軍領司馬，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanxi, when Grand General Jiang Wan campaigned to Hanzhong, Fu as former army supervisor concurrent marshal died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yanxi, when Jiang Wan marched to Hanzhong, Li Fu went as former army supervisor and chief marshal—and died on duty.

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆舊雜記曰：諸葛亮於武功病篤，後主遣福省侍，遂因諮以國家大計。

translations.literal: The Yibu Qi Jiu Za Ji says: When Zhuge Liang was gravely ill at Wugong, the Later Lord sent Fu to visit and nurse him, and thereby consult on the great plans of state.
translations.idiomatic: The Yibu Qi Jiu Za Ji says that when Zhuge Liang lay dying at Wugong, the emperor sent Li Fu to his bedside both to inquire after him and to ask the great question of succession.

sentences.zh: 福往具宣聖旨，聽亮所言，至別去數日，忽馳思未盡其意，遂卻騎馳還見亮。

translations.literal: Fu went and fully announced the sage edict, listened to what Liang said, and when parting had gone several days, suddenly galloped thinking he had not exhausted the meaning, then turned his mount and galloped back to see Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu delivered the imperial message, heard Liang out, and rode away—but after a few days realized he had left something unsaid and galloped back to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 亮語福曰：「孤知君還意。

translations.literal: Liang said to Fu: "I know the intent of your return."
translations.idiomatic: Liang greeted him with, "I know why you have come back."

sentences.zh: 近日言語，雖彌日有所不盡，更來一決耳。

translations.literal: "These recent words, though for a full day there was something not exhausted, coming again is one final settling."
translations.idiomatic: "We spoke a full day yet did not finish; you have returned for one last word."

sentences.zh: 君所問者，公琰其宜也。

translations.literal: What you ask—Gongyan is the fitting one.
translations.idiomatic: For what you wish to know—Jiang Wan is the right man.

sentences.zh: 」福謝：「前實失不諮請公，如公百年後，誰可任大事者？

translations.literal: Fu apologized: "Before I truly failed to ask: if you, sir, after a hundred years, who can undertake great affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu apologized: "I should have asked plainly—after your death, who can bear the greatest burden?"

sentences.zh: 故輒還耳。

translations.literal: Therefore I abruptly returned.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I turned back."

sentences.zh: 乞復請，蔣琬之後，誰可任者？

translations.literal: I beg to ask again: after Jiang Wan, who can be entrusted?"
translations.idiomatic: May I ask further—after Jiang Wan, who comes next?"

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「文偉可以繼之。

translations.literal: Liang said: "Wenwei can succeed him."
translations.idiomatic: Liang answered, "Fei Yi can follow him."

sentences.zh: 」又復問其次，亮不答。

translations.literal: He again asked who was next; Liang did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu pressed for a third name, Liang fell silent.

sentences.zh: 福還，奉使稱旨。

translations.literal: Fu returned and on mission matched the edict's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu returned and reported in full accord with the emperor’s charge.

sentences.zh: 福為人精識果銳，敏於從政。

translations.literal: Fu as a person was keen in judgment, decisive and sharp, quick in handling government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu was shrewd, decisive, and swift in administration.

sentences.zh: 子驤，字叔龍，亦有名，官至尚書郎、廣漢太守。〉

translations.literal: His son Xiang, courtesy name Shulong, also had reputation; his office reached Gentleman of the Ministers and Administrator of Guanghan.〉
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang, style Shulong, also made a name and rose to gentleman in the ministry and Administrator of Guanghan.〉

sentences.zh: 偉南名朝，永南兄。

translations.literal: Weinan’s given name was Chao; he was Yongnan’s elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chao, style Weinan, was the elder brother of Li Shao.

sentences.zh: 郡功曹，舉孝廉，臨邛令，入為別駕從事。

translations.literal: County merit officer, recommended Filial and Incorrupt, magistrate of Linqiong, entered as Adjunct Clerk for Separate Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He served as county merit officer, was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, governed Linqiong, and became separate-carriage chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 隨先主東征吳，章武二年卒於永安。

translations.literal: He followed the First Sovereign on the eastern campaign against Wu and in the second year of Zhangwu died at Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He marched east against Wu with the First Sovereign and died at Yong’an in Zhangwu 2.

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆舊雜記曰：朝又有一弟，早亡，各有才望，時人號之李氏三龍。

translations.literal: The Yibu Qi Jiu Za Ji says: Chao also had one younger brother who died early; each had talent and reputation, and people of the time called them the Three Dragons of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Yibu Qi Jiu Za Ji adds that Chao had a talented younger brother who died young; contemporaries called the three brothers the Li clan’s “three dragons.”

sentences.zh: 《華陽國志》曰：群下上先主為漢中王；

translations.literal: The Huayang Guozhi says: The subordinates memorialized the First Sovereign to be King of Hanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang Guozhi records that the court memorialized Liu Bei as king of Hanzhong;

sentences.zh: 其文，朝所造也。

translations.literal: its text was composed by Chao.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Chao drafted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案耆舊所記，以朝、邵及早亡者為三龍。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi examines what the Qi Jiu recorded, taking Chao, Shao, and the early-deceased one as the three dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that the old record counts Li Chao, Li Shao, and their early-deceased brother as the three dragons.

sentences.zh: 邈之狂直，不得在此數。〉

translations.literal: Li Miao's mad bluntness does not belong in this number.〉
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao’s wild temper keeps him out of that company.〉

sentences.zh: 德緒名祿，巴西安漢人也。

translations.literal: Dexu’s given name was Lu; he was a man of Anhan in Ba command.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Lu, style Dexu, came from Anhan in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，為郡從事牙門將。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign settled Yizhou he was county Adjunct and Colonel of the Gateguards.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhou fell he served as county adjutant and gateguards colonel.

sentences.zh: 建興三年，為越巂太守，隨丞相亮南征，為蠻夷所害，時年三十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianxing he was Administrator of Yuexi and followed Chancellor Liang on the southern campaign; he was killed by the Man and Yi barbarians at age thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 3 he was Administrator of Yuexi and followed Zhuge Liang south; barbarians killed him at thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 弟衡，景耀中為領軍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Heng in the Jingyao era was Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Heng became commander of the army under Jingyao.

sentences.zh: 義強名士，廣漢郪人，國山從兄也。

translations.literal: Yiqiang’s given name was Shi; he was a man of Qi in Guanghan, Guoshan’s elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, style Yiqiang, from Qi in Guanghan, was Wang Guo’s elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 從先主入蜀後，舉孝廉，為符節長，遷牙門將，出為宕渠太守，徙在犍為。

translations.literal: After following the First Sovereign into Shu he was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, became magistrate of tally and tallies, was moved up to Colonel of the Gateguards, went out as Administrator of Dangqu, and was transferred to Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Shu with Liu Bei, was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, rose from tally magistrate to gateguards colonel, governed Dangqu, and was shifted to Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 會丞相亮南征，轉為益州太守，將南行，為蠻夷所害。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Liang campaigned south he was transferred to Administrator of Yizhou; about to march south he was killed by the Man and Yi barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang marched south he was named Administrator of Yizhou; he was killed by tribesmen before the column moved.

sentences.zh: 休元輕寇，損時致害，

translations.literal: Xiuyuan treated the enemy lightly, harmed the moment and brought disaster,
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi underrated the foe and paid for it with his life,

sentences.zh: 文進奮身，同此顛沛，

translations.literal: Wenjin threw himself forward, sharing this overturning,
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Nan rushed in and shared the same ruin,

sentences.zh: 患生一人，至於弘大。

translations.literal: trouble arising in one man extends to the vast and great.
translations.idiomatic: one man’s misjudgment swelled into a great catastrophe.

sentences.zh: ──贊馮休元、張文進

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Feng Xiuyuan and Zhang Wenjin
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Feng Xi and Zhang Nan

sentences.zh: 休元名習，南郡人。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan’s given name was Xi; he was a man of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi, style Xiuyuan, came from Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 隨先主入蜀。

translations.literal: He followed the First Sovereign into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Liu Bei into Shu.

sentences.zh: 先主東征吳，習為領軍，統諸軍，大敗於猇亭。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign campaigned east against Wu, Xi was Commander of the Army, directing the various armies, and was greatly defeated at Xiaoting.
translations.idiomatic: On the Wu campaign he commanded the army and met the great defeat at Xiaoting.

sentences.zh: 文進名南，亦自荊州隨先主入蜀，領兵從先主徵吳，與習俱死。

translations.literal: Wenjin’s given name was Nan; he likewise from Jingzhou followed the First Sovereign into Shu, led troops following the First Sovereign on the campaign against Wu, and with Xi both died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Nan, style Wenjin, also from Jingzhou, followed Liu Bei into Shu, led troops on the Wu campaign, and died beside Feng Xi.

sentences.zh: 時又有義陽傅肜，先主退軍，斷後拒戰，兵人死盡，吳將語肜令降，肜罵曰：「吳狗！

translations.literal: At the time there was also Fu Rong of Yiyang; when the First Sovereign withdrew the army he covered the rear and fought; soldiers were all dead; a Wu general told Rong to surrender, and Rong cursed, saying: "Wu dogs!"
translations.idiomatic: There was also Fu Rong of Yiyang, who covered the retreat when Liu Bei withdrew; when his men were gone a Wu officer demanded his surrender, and Rong snarled, "Dogs of Wu!"

sentences.zh: 何有漢將軍降者！

translations.literal: How can there be a Han general who surrenders!"
translations.idiomatic: What Han general ever surrenders to you!"

sentences.zh: 」遂戰死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on until he fell.

sentences.zh: 拜子僉為左中郎，後為關中都督，景耀六年，又臨危授命。

translations.literal: His son Qian was appointed General of the Household of the Left; afterward he became Area Commander of Guanzhong; in the sixth year of Jingyao he again on peril entrusted his life.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian was made general of the household of the left, later Guanzhong area commander, and in Jingyao 6 again died accepting a fatal charge.

sentences.zh: 論者嘉其父子奕世忠義。

translations.literal: Discussers praised father and son for successive generations of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Critics praised the father and son for loyalty handed down through two generations.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記載晉武帝詔曰：「蜀將軍傅僉，前在關城，身拒官軍，致死不顧。

translations.literal: The Shu Ji records an edict of Jin Emperor Wu saying: "The Shu general Fu Qian, formerly at Guan city, personally resisted imperial troops and died without turning aside.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji preserves Jin Emperor Wu’s edict: "The Shu general Fu Qian held Guan city against my army and died without flinching.

sentences.zh: 僉父肜，復為劉備戰亡。

translations.literal: Qian's father Rong again died fighting for Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong had already died fighting for Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 天下之善一也，豈由彼此以為異？

translations.literal: The good in the empire is one—how can we make it different by this or that side!"
translations.idiomatic: Virtue is one under heaven—why should we draw a line between your side and mine!"

sentences.zh: 」僉息著、募，後沒入奚官，免為庶人。〉

translations.literal: Qian's sons Zhu and Mu afterward were taken into the eunuch bureau, exempted to commoner status.〉
translations.idiomatic: Qian’s sons Zhu and Mu were later impressed into the palace bureau but eventually freed to commoner status.〉

sentences.zh: 江陽剛烈，立節明君，

translations.literal: Jiangyang was stern and fierce; he set integrity before an enlightened lord,
translations.idiomatic: The man of Jiangyang was iron in temper—he set his honor before his king,

sentences.zh: 兵合遇寇，不屈其身，

translations.literal: arms joined, met the bandit, and would not bend his person,
translations.idiomatic: met the foe with ranks closed and would not bend,

sentences.zh: 單夫只役，隕命於軍。

translations.literal: a lone husband with only servants—he threw away life in the army.
translations.idiomatic: a single man with a handful of men—he gave his life on the field.

sentences.zh: ──贊程季然

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Cheng Jiran
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Cheng Ji

sentences.zh: 季然名畿，巴西閬中人也。

translations.literal: Jiran’s given name was Ji; he was a man of Langzhong in Ba command.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji, style Jiran, came from Langzhong in Ba.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時為漢昌長。

translations.literal: Under Liu Zhang he was magistrate of Hanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he governed Hanchang.

sentences.zh: 縣有賨人，種類剛猛，昔高祖以定關中。

translations.literal: The county had Cong people, a type fierce and stubborn; in olden days the High Ancestor used them to settle Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The county held Cong tribesmen, a tough people the High Founder had once used to secure Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 巴西太守龐羲以天下擾亂，郡宜有武衛，頗招合部曲。

translations.literal: Administrator of Ba Pang Xi, because the empire was disturbed and chaotic, thought the commandery ought to have martial guard, and widely recruited and assembled personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xi the Administrator of Ba, seeing the realm in turmoil, decided the commandery needed an armed guard and raised a large private following.

sentences.zh: 有讒於璋，說羲欲叛者，璋陰疑之。

translations.literal: There was slander toward Zhang saying Xi wished to rebel; Zhang secretly suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Pang Xi to Liu Zhang as a would-be rebel, and Zhang began to doubt him.

sentences.zh: 羲聞，甚懼，將謀自守，遣畿子鬱宣旨，索兵自助。

translations.literal: Xi hearing was greatly afraid and planned to hold himself in defense; he sent Ji's son Yu to announce intent and request troops to aid himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xi panicked and prepared to hold out; he sent Ji’s son Yu with a message begging Ji to send troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 畿報曰：「郡合部曲，本不為叛，雖有交構，要在盡誠；

translations.literal: Ji replied, saying: "The commandery assembling personal troops was originally not for rebellion; though there is intrigue, the essential thing is to exhaust good faith;
translations.idiomatic: Ji answered, "You raised troops for defense, not treason; though rumor flies, good faith is still the cure;

sentences.zh: 若必以懼，遂懷異志，非畿之所聞。

translations.literal: if out of fear you then harbor a different intent, it is not what Ji has heard of."
translations.idiomatic: if fear drives you to disloyalty, I have never heard of such a course ending well."

sentences.zh: 」並敕鬱曰：「我受州恩，當為州牧盡節。

translations.literal: He also instructed Yu, saying: "I have received the province's kindness and ought to exhaust integrity for the shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: He warned Yu, "The province has been good to me; I owe my life to its shepherd.

sentences.zh: 汝為郡吏，當為太守效力，不得以吾故有異志也。

translations.literal: You are a county clerk and ought to exert strength for the administrator; you may not because of me have a different intent."
translations.idiomatic: You are a county officer—you owe your duty to the administrator, not to me."

sentences.zh: 」羲使人告畿曰：「爾子在郡，不從太守，家將及禍！

translations.literal: Xi sent a man to tell Ji: "Your son is in the commandery and will not obey the administrator—your household will meet calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent word: "Your son defies the administrator—your whole house will suffer!"

sentences.zh: 」畿曰：「昔樂羊為將，飲子之羹，非父子無恩，大義然也。

translations.literal: Ji said: "In olden days Yue Yang as general drank his son's soup; it was not that father and son lacked kindness—great righteousness was thus."
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "Yue Yang the general drank soup made from his own son—not from lack of love, but from duty to the state."

sentences.zh: 今雖復羹子，吾必飲之。

translations.literal: Now though again they should make soup of a son, I would be sure to drink it."
translations.idiomatic: Even if they boiled another bowl from my own flesh, I would still drink it."

sentences.zh: 」羲知畿必不為己，厚陳謝於璋以致無咎。

translations.literal: Xi knew Ji would certainly not act for himself, and richly stated apology to Zhang so as to bring about no blame.
translations.idiomatic: Xi saw that Ji would never serve a private plot and made his peace with Liu Zhang through abject apology.

sentences.zh: 璋聞之，遷畿江陽太守。

translations.literal: Zhang hearing of it moved Ji to Administrator of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang then transferred Ji to Administrator of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 先主領益州牧，闢為從事祭酒。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign held the shepherdcy of Yizhou he summoned him as Libationer Adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei became shepherd of Yizhou he named Ji libationer-adjunct.

sentences.zh: 後隨先主徵吳，遇大軍敗績，溯江而還，或告之曰：「後追已至，解船輕去，乃可以免。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed the First Sovereign on the campaign against Wu, met the great army's rout, and went back upstream; someone told him: "The rear pursuers have already arrived—cast off the boats lightly and go, then you can escape."
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Wu with Liu Bei, survived the great rout, and was rowing upstream when someone cried, "The pursuers are here—abandon the boats and run!"

sentences.zh: 」畿曰：「吾在軍，未曾為敵走，況從天子而見危哉！

translations.literal: Ji said: "I in the army have never for the enemy fled; how much more following the Son of Heaven and seeing peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji answered, "I have never fled a foe in the field—would I flee now beside my emperor?"

sentences.zh: 」追人遂及畿船，畿身執戟戰，敵船有覆者。

translations.literal: The pursuers then reached Ji's boat; Ji personally grasped halberd and fought; enemy boats had capsized ones.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy overtook his boat; he seized a halberd and fought until enemy craft overturned.

sentences.zh: 眾大至，共擊之，乃死。

translations.literal: The multitude greatly arrived; together they struck him, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When overwhelming numbers closed in, they cut him down.

sentences.zh: 公弘後生，卓爾奇精，

translations.literal: Gonghong, born after, outstanding and wondrously keen,
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qi, born after him, stood out as a prodigy,

sentences.zh: 夭命二十，悼恨未呈。

translations.literal: heaven's mandate twenty, grief and regret not yet displayed.
translations.idiomatic: yet heaven gave him only twenty years—grief that his promise never ripened.

sentences.zh: ──贊程公弘

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Cheng Gonghong
translations.idiomatic: ──In praise of Cheng Qi

sentences.zh: 公弘，名祁，季然之子也。

translations.literal: Gonghong, given name Qi, was Ji's son.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qi, style Gonghong, was Cheng Ji’s son.

sentences.zh: 古之奔臣，禮有來偪，

translations.literal: The fleeing minister of olden days—by ritual there is the coming pressure,
translations.idiomatic: The turncoat of old—ritual knows the press of circumstance,

sentences.zh: 怨興司官，不顧大德。

translations.literal: resentment rising toward the responsible official, not looking to great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: yet nursed grudges against his superiors and forgot the greater good.

sentences.zh: 靡有匡救，倍成奔北，

translations.literal: There was none to rescue and aid; doubly they accomplished fleeing north,
translations.idiomatic: No one could save them; they doubled their flight northward,

sentences.zh: 自絕於人，作笑二國。

translations.literal: cutting themselves off from men, making laughter for two states.
translations.idiomatic: cut themselves off from honor and became a jest to two kingdoms.

sentences.zh: ──贊糜芳、士仁、郝普、潘濬

translations.literal: ──Encomium on Mi Fang, Shi Ren, Hao Pu, and Pan Jun
translations.idiomatic: ──On Mi Fang, Shi Ren, Hao Pu, and Pan Jun

sentences.zh: 糜芳字子方，東海人也，為南郡太守。

translations.literal: Mi Fang, courtesy name Zifang, was a man of Donghai; he was Administrator of Nan command.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Fang, style Zifang, from Donghai, was Administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 士仁字君義，廣陽人也，為將軍，住公安，統屬關羽；

translations.literal: Shi Ren, courtesy name Junyi, was a man of Guangyang; he was a general stationed at Gongan, under Guan Yu's command;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ren, style Junyi, from Guangyang, was a general at Gongan under Guan Yu’s command;

sentences.zh: 與羽有隙，叛迎孫權。

translations.literal: having a rift with Yu, he rebelled and welcomed Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: he fell out with Yu and opened the gates to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 郝普字子太，義陽人。

translations.literal: Hao Pu, courtesy name Zitai, was a man of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Pu, style Zitai, came from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 先主自荊州入蜀，以普為零陵太守。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign from Jingzhou entered Shu he made Pu Administrator of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei left for Shu he left Pu as Administrator of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 為吳將呂蒙所譎，開城詣蒙。

translations.literal: He was deceived by the Wu general Lü Meng and opened the city to go to Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng tricked him into opening Lingling and yielding to Wu.

sentences.zh: 潘濬字承明，武陵人也。

translations.literal: Pan Jun, courtesy name Chengming, was a man of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jun, style Chengming, was a native of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 先主入蜀，以為荊州治中，典留州事，亦與關羽不穆。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign entered Shu he made him provincial Adjunct Clerk for the Headquarters, in charge of affairs of the province left behind, and he likewise was not harmonious with Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei made him chief clerk of the Jingzhou rear headquarters; he too could not work with Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 孫權襲羽，遂入吳。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan raided Yu, he thereupon entered Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan struck Guan Yu, he went over to Wu.

sentences.zh: 普至廷尉，濬至太常，封侯。

translations.literal: Pu reached Commandant of Justice; Jun reached Minister of Ceremonies; both were enfeoffed marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Pu rose to commandant of justice and Pan Jun to minister of rites; both received marquisates.

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆舊雜記載王嗣、常播、衛繼三人，皆劉氏王蜀時人，故錄於篇。

translations.literal: The Yibu Qi Jiu Za Ji records three men—Wang Si, Chang Bo, and Wei Ji—all people of the Liu clan’s royal Shu period; therefore they are recorded in the chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The Yibu Qi Jiu Za Ji preserves three minor figures—Wang Si, Chang Bo, and Wei Ji—from the Liu regime in Shu, and they are appended here.

sentences.zh: 王嗣字承宗，犍為資中人也。

translations.literal: Wang Si, courtesy name Chengzong, was a man of Zizhong in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si, style Chengzong, came from Zizhong in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 其先，延熙世以功德顯著。

translations.literal: His ancestors in the Yanxi era by merit and virtue were conspicuously notable.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had won distinction for service during the Yanxi years.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，稍遷西安圍督、汶山太守，加安遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, was gradually moved up to Colonel Who Garrisons Xi'an, Administrator of Wenshan, and additionally General Who Pacifies the Far.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended Filial and Incorrupt, he rose to colonel at Xi’an, Administrator of Wenshan, and General Who Pacifies the Far.

sentences.zh: 綏集羌、胡，咸悉歸服，諸種素桀惡者皆來首降，嗣待以恩信，時北境得以寧靜。

translations.literal: He soothed and gathered Qiang and Hu; all submitted and returned to allegiance; the various kinds that by nature had been obstinate and evil all came to offer surrender first; Si treated them with grace and trust, so that at the time the northern marches could obtain quiet and calm.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Qiang and Hu until every tribe submitted—even the most truculent came in first to surrender—and ruled them with kindness until the northern frontier grew still.

sentences.zh: 大將軍姜維每出北征，羌、胡出馬牛羊氈毦及義谷裨軍糧，國賴其資。

translations.literal: Grand General Jiang Wei whenever went out on northern campaign, Qiang and Hu supplied horses, oxen, sheep, felt, and grain as righteous grain to aid the army's provisions, and the state relied on their resources.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jiang Wei marched north, those peoples sent horses, cattle, sheep, felt, and grain for his commissary, and the state leaned heavily on their tribute.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮軍，故領郡。

translations.literal: He was moved to General Who Guards the Army and as before concurrently held the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who guards the army while keeping his commandery post.

sentences.zh: 後從維北征，為流矢所傷，數月卒。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed Wei on the northern campaign, was wounded by a stray arrow, and after several months died.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wei north, took a stray arrow, and died within a few months.

sentences.zh: 戎夷會葬，贈送數千人，號呼涕泣。

translations.literal: Rong and Yi assembled for the funeral; gifts were sent by several thousand persons; they cried out and wept tears.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier peoples thronged his funeral; thousands brought gifts, wailing aloud.

sentences.zh: 嗣為人美厚篤至，眾所愛信。

translations.literal: Si as a person was beautiful, thick, and earnest to the utmost; the multitude loved and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si was generous and steadfast; everyone loved and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 嗣子及孫，羌、胡見之如骨肉，或結兄弟，恩至於此。

translations.literal: Si's sons and grandsons—when Qiang and Hu saw them it was like flesh and bone, or they bonded as brothers; grace reached this extent.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and grandsons were greeted by Qiang and Hu as kin—some even swore brotherhood—such was the depth of his grace.

sentences.zh: 常播字文平，蜀郡江原人也。

translations.literal: Chang Bo, courtesy name Wenping, was a man of Jiangyuan in Shujun.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Bo, style Wenping, came from Jiangyuan in Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 播仕縣主簿功曹。

translations.literal: Bo served the county as chief clerk and merit officer.
translations.idiomatic: Bo served his county as chief clerk and merit officer.

sentences.zh: 縣長廣都硃遊，建興十五年中被上官誣劾以逋沒官谷，當論重罪。

translations.literal: The county magistrate Zhu You of Guangdu, in the middle of the fifteenth year of Jianxing, was by a superior official falsely impeached for defaulting on official grain and ought to be sentenced to heavy crime.
translations.idiomatic: In mid–Jianxing 15 the magistrate Zhu You of Guangdu was framed by a superior for embezzling official grain and faced a capital charge.

sentences.zh: 播詣獄訟爭，身受數千杖，肌膚刻爛，毒痛慘至，更曆三獄，幽閉二年有餘。

translations.literal: Bo went to prison to argue the lawsuit; his body received several thousand blows of the staff; flesh and skin were carved and rotted; poison pain reached the utmost extreme; he passed through three prisons, confined in darkness more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: Bo went to jail to plead Zhu’s case, took thousands of strokes until his flesh hung in strips, and spent over two years shut through three prisons.

sentences.zh: 每將考掠，吏先驗問，播不答，言「但急行罰，無所多問」！

translations.literal: Whenever they were about to examine and flog, the clerks first verified and questioned; Bo did not answer, saying "Only hurry to carry out punishment—there is nothing more to question!"
translations.idiomatic: Before each flogging the clerks questioned him, but he would only say, "Beat me and have done—there is nothing to ask!"

sentences.zh: 辭終不撓，事遂分明。

translations.literal: His words to the end were not bent; the affair thereupon became clear.
translations.idiomatic: He never broke, and the truth finally came out.

sentences.zh: 長免刑戮。

translations.literal: The magistrate was spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 時唯主簿楊玩亦證明其事，與播辭同。

translations.literal: At the time only Chief Clerk Yang Wan likewise proved clear the affair; his words matched Bo's.
translations.idiomatic: Only chief clerk Yang Wan stood with him and told the same story.

sentences.zh: 眾咸嘉播忘身為君，節義抗烈。

translations.literal: The multitude all praised Bo for forgetting his person for his lord; his integrity and righteousness resisted fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: All praised Bo for risking his life for his magistrate—his integrity blazed like fire.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，除郪長，年五十餘卒。

translations.literal: He was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, was appointed magistrate of Qi, and died at a little more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended Filial and Incorrupt, he became magistrate of Qi and died in his fifties.

sentences.zh: 書於舊德傳，後縣令潁川趙敦圖其像，讚頌之。

translations.literal: It is written in the Traditions of Old Virtue; afterward County Magistrate Zhao Dun of Yingchuan painted his likeness and composed praise for him.
translations.idiomatic: His name was entered in the Traditions of Old Virtue, and later Magistrate Zhao Dun of Yingchuan painted his portrait and wrote his praise.

sentences.zh: 衛繼字子業，漢嘉嚴道人也。

translations.literal: Wei Ji, courtesy name Ziye, was a man of Yandao in Hanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji, style Ziye, came from Yandao in Hanjia.

sentences.zh: 兄弟五人。

translations.literal: There were five brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He was one of five brothers.

sentences.zh: 繼父為縣功曹。

translations.literal: Ji's father was county merit officer.
translations.idiomatic: Ji’s father was the county merit officer.

sentences.zh: 繼為兒時，與兄弟隨父遊戲庭寺中，縣長蜀郡成都張君無子，數命功曹呼其子省弄，甚憐愛之。

translations.literal: When Ji was a child, together with brothers he followed his father playing in the county courtyard; the county magistrate, Zhang Jun of Chengdu in Shujun, had no sons and repeatedly ordered the merit officer to call his sons in for him to look at and dote on them, greatly pitying and loving them.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Ji played in the yamen with his brothers while his father worked; the childless magistrate Zhang Jun of Chengdu kept calling the boys in to dote on them.

sentences.zh: 張因言宴之間，語功曹欲乞繼，功曹即許之，遂養為子。

translations.literal: Zhang therefore at a banquet spoke to the merit officer wishing to beg Ji; the merit officer immediately promised it, and Zhang thereupon raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast Zhang asked to adopt Ji; the merit officer agreed, and Zhang raised him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 繼敏達夙成，學識通博，進仕州郡，歷職清顯。

translations.literal: Ji was quick and penetrating, mature from youth; learning and knowledge were thorough and broad; he advanced in office in province and commandery, passing through posts pure and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was precocious, learned, and rose through provincial posts of unimpeachable rank.

sentences.zh: 而其餘兄弟四人，各無堪當世者，父恆言己之將衰，張明府將盛也。

translations.literal: But his remaining four brothers each had none who could match the age; his father constantly said that his own line would decline and Prefect Zhang's line would flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his four natural brothers showed no talent; his father used to sigh that his own line was fading while Magistrate Zhang’s would flourish.

sentences.zh: 時法禁以異姓為後，故復為衛氏。

translations.literal: At the time the law forbade taking a different surname as heir; therefore he again became of the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: The law barred adoption under an alien surname, so he resumed the name Wei.

sentences.zh: 屢遷拜奉車都尉、大尚書，忠篤信厚，為眾所敬。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly moved and appointed Colonel Who Leads the Household Carriages and Grand Minister; loyal, earnest, trustworthy, and thick—he was what the multitude revered.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel of the household carriages and grand minister, loyal and staid, and universally respected.

sentences.zh: 鍾會之亂，遇害成都。〉

translations.literal: In Zhong Hui's rebellion he met death at Chengdu.〉
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chengdu during Zhong Hui’s mutiny.〉

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：鄧芝堅貞簡亮，臨官忘家，張翼亢姜維之銳，宗預禦孫權之嚴，咸有可稱。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Deng Zhi was firm, chaste, spare, and bright; facing office he forgot his family; Zhang Yi withstood Jiang Wei's keen edge; Zong Yu parried Sun Quan's severity—all had what is praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Deng Zhi was incorruptible and plain, forgetting self for duty; Zhang Yi defied Jiang Wei’s edge; Zong Yu matched Sun Quan’s sternness—each deserves mention.

sentences.zh: 楊戲商略，意在不群，然智度有短，殆罹世難雲。

translations.literal: Yang Xi weighed and summarized, his intent being not to flock with the crowd; yet in wisdom and measure he had shortcomings, and probably met the age's hardships, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xi aimed to stand apart in judgment and style, yet his judgment fell short and he nearly perished in the troubles of his time.
